profiles.business_description: Insight Enterprises is a Fortune 500 IT solutions integrator (distributor + services), serving enterprise and public-sector clients across hardware, software, and cloud services. Business is organized in three geographic segments: North America (81% of revenue), EMEA (16%), and APAC (3%). Revenue mix is heavily product-distribution (hardware/software resale) with a growing managed services layer. From a credit perspective, NSIT is a low-leverage distributor credit (0.3x net leverage, $358MM cash) with $500MM 6.625% Senior Notes due 2032 and a $2B ABL facility as primary liquidity.

profiles.business_description: Enviri Corporation (ticker: NVRI) is a global provider of environmental solutions operating three segments: Harsco Environmental (onsite industrial waste services for the metals industry), Clean Earth (specialty hazardous/non-hazardous waste processing), and Harsco Rail (railway track maintenance equipment and services). The company has signed a definitive agreement to sell its Clean Earth segment to Veolia for over $3 billion, with the remaining Harsco Environmental and Harsco Rail businesses to be spun off as a standalone public company ('New Enviri'). Post-transaction, the credit profile will be materially restructured around two smaller, more focused segments.

The chemicals business benefits from integration across the ECU value chain, while Winchester serves commercial, law enforcement, and military customers with a significant government contract base including operation of the Lake City Army Ammunition Plant. All three segments are capital-intensive manufacturing businesses exposed to commodity input costs and cyclical end markets.

profiles.business_description: onsemi (ON Semiconductor) is a leading provider of intelligent power and intelligent sensing solutions targeting automotive, industrial, and AI data center markets, with $6.0B FY2025 revenue (down 15% YoY from $7.1B). profiles.business_description: OpenText is a Canadian information management software company, transformed by the $6B acquisition of Micro Focus (Jan 2023) into one of the largest enterprise software companies globally. Products span content management, digital experience, security/compliance (Voltage, ArcSight), and business network. Total revenue was $5.17B in FY2025 (-10% YoY post-AMC divestiture), with $4.19B in annual recurring revenue (ARR). Cloud services and subscriptions grew 2% to $1.86B. Credit relevance: $6.3B total debt (7.1x gross leverage) from Micro Focus financing is the dominant credit consideration; deleveraging pace and EBITDA margin recovery from integration are key watch items.

profiles.business_description: Otis is the world's leading elevator and escalator manufacturing, installation, service, and modernization company, serving customers in over 200 countries and territories. The company operates two segments: New Equipment (35% of net sales), which designs, manufactures, and installs elevators and escalators, and Service (65% of net sales), which provides maintenance, repair, and modernization services for approximately 2.5 million units globally. From a creditor perspective, the high-margin, recurring Service segment provides significant cash flow stability, partially offsetting cyclicality in the New Equipment segment tied to global construction activity.

profiles.business_description: PBF Holding Company LLC is an independent petroleum refiner operating six oil refineries with a combined throughput capacity of approximately 1 million barrels per day. Facilities span the US East Coast (Delaware City, DE; Paulsboro, NJ), Gulf Coast (Chalmette, LA), Mid-Continent (Toledo, OH), and West Coast (Torrance and Martinez, CA). PBF is the largest independent refiner by East Coast capacity. Revenue of $29.3B LTM reflects the massive throughput volume, though EBITDA varies dramatically with crack spreads -- from sub-$500M at trough to $3B+ at peak. The company has no crude production, making it a pure refining margin play. The ABL credit facility is secured by inventory and receivables. PBF also holds a logistics MLP (PBFX) providing pipeline and storage infrastructure.

profiles.business_description: Pitney Bowes is a technology-driven shipping and mailing company serving over 90% of the Fortune 500, structured around two continuing segments after the 2024 wind-down of Global Ecommerce. SendTech Solutions provides physical and digital mailing/shipping technology, financing, and postage management; revenue is in structural decline as enterprise mail volumes compress. Presort Services is the largest USPS workshare partner, offering first-mile sortation that captures postal discounts for clients. The ecommerce exit removes a $300MM+ annual loss drag but leaves a mature, cash-generative but secularly shrinking core. Credit relevance centers on $1.99B of debt, 4.2x net leverage, and a springing maturity on $368MM of Notes due March 2027 that could accelerate the secured term loans if not refinanced by September 2026.

profiles.business_description: PHINIA Inc. is a global designer and manufacturer of fuel injection systems, fuel delivery modules, electronic control modules, and aftermarket parts for combustion and hybrid propulsion systems across commercial vehicles, light vehicles, and industrial applications. Spun off from BorgWarner in July 2023, the company serves major OEMs and the independent aftermarket through two segments: Fuel Systems (~67% of revenue) and Aftermarket (~37% of revenue). With ~$3.5B in annual net sales and significant international exposure (63% outside the U.S.), PHINIA faces secular headwinds from ICE-to-EV transition but benefits from a large installed base, aftermarket demand, and hybrid/alternative fuel growth.

profiles.business_description: Park-Ohio Holdings Corp. is a diversified international manufacturer and supply chain services provider operating through three segments: Supply Technologies (supply chain management outsourcing for production components), Assembly Components (fuel system and rubber/plastic assemblies for automotive/light vehicle), and Engineered Products (induction heating/melting systems, pipe threading, forged/machined products). The company serves a broad range of industrial end markets including heavy-duty truck, automotive, aerospace/defense, oil & gas, and construction equipment, with approximately $1.6 billion in revenue and ~6,300 employees globally. From a creditor perspective, the company carries meaningful leverage (~58% net debt to capitalization) with $635.7 million in gross debt, including $350 million in 8.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 and a $405 million revolving credit facility.

profiles.business_description: Permian Resources Operating LLC (formerly Centennial Resource Development, merged with Earthstone Energy in 2023) is a large-scale Delaware Basin E&P producing approximately 350,000 boepd, making it one of the largest pure-play Permian operators. The company operates primarily in Reeves, Ward, and Loving Counties, Texas, with a deep multi-bench inventory in the Wolfcamp, Bone Spring, and Third Bone Spring formations. The Earthstone merger created significant scale advantages in contiguous acreage, enabling longer laterals and capital efficiency improvements. LTM revenue of $5.07B and EBITDA of $3.69B on the combined platform. The revolver is fully undrawn with $2.6B+ total liquidity. PR is the closest credit in the E&P coverage to formal IG rating.
profiles.end_markets: ["Crude Oil Production", "Natural Gas", "NGL Processing", "Permian Basin Development"]
profiles.geographic_mix: US 100% (Delaware Basin, Permian - Reeves, Ward, Loving Counties, TX)
profiles.competitive_position: top-tier Delaware Basin operator; post-Earthstone merger scale creates capital efficiency advantage

profiles.business_description: Perimeter Solutions is a leading provider of niche industrial products and services across two segments: Fire Safety (fire retardants, suppressants, equipment, and services for wildland, industrial, and structural firefighting) and Specialty Products (P2S5-based lubricant additives, electronic/electro-mechanical components via IMS, and, following the January 2026 acquisition of MMT, highly engineered machinery for medical device manufacturing). The company serves primarily government agencies and industrial customers globally, with ~76% of revenues from the U.S. Its capital allocation strategy prioritizes organic reinvestment, share repurchases, and acquisitions, with a stated goal of generating private-equity-like returns.

Free cash flow of $857M in FY25 (16% growth) supports aggressive deleveraging: net debt repayments of $553M and $300M share buybacks in FY25. The pending Kepware/ThingWorx divestiture will generate up to $600M at close expected H1 2026, further strengthening the balance sheet.

profiles.business_description: Transocean International Ltd is the world's largest offshore drilling contractor by fleet size, operating ultra-deepwater drillships and harsh-environment semi-submersible drilling rigs. The company's fleet serves major oil companies (Equinor, Petrobras, Chevron, Shell, BP) across global deepwater basins including Gulf of Mexico, Brazil pre-salt, West Africa, and North Sea. Revenue of $3.97B LTM. Transocean carries a massive legacy debt load from the 2014-2020 offshore downturn, though active deleveraging has reduced total debt by ~$1.3B YoY. The 8.75% secured notes have a 5-rig collateral package. Contract backlog provides multi-year revenue visibility as the deepwater cycle improves.

profiles.business_description: RingCentral is the leading UCaaS platform provider, offering AI-powered cloud communications (RingEX), contact center (RingCX/RingCentral Contact Center powered by NICE), video, and agentic voice AI. ARR reached $2.67B as of December 2025 (+7% YoY). The company serves enterprise clients with carrier-grade reliability across 45 countries. The critical credit challenge is the $609M 2026 Convertible Notes maturing March 2026 -- requiring refinancing or cash settlement against only $132M cash on hand. Total debt is $1.26B comprising the 2026 converts, $302M term loan (due 2030), and $350M 8.5% Senior Notes (due 2030). The company generated $2.5B total revenue in FY25 with improving margins (SBC declining from 14% to 11% of revenue) but remains in a stockholders deficit of $588M from prior losses.

profiles.business_description: Range Resources Corporation is a pure-play Appalachian natural gas E&P operating exclusively in the Marcellus Shale in southwestern Pennsylvania. The company is one of the original Marcellus developers and operates some of the most economic acreage in the basin with super-rich, wet, and dry gas drilling locations. Range operates the Martica NGL complex for fractionation and export, adding NGL revenue diversification to the pure-gas base. LTM revenue of $2.99B and EBITDA of $1.32B. The company generates exceptional free cash flow ($1.02B LTM) at relatively low capex intensity compared to Permian oil peers. Range's sub-$1.75/mcf full-cycle breakeven is among the lowest in US gas, providing wide margin of safety through commodity cycles.
profiles.end_markets: ["Natural Gas Production", "NGL Processing & Export (Martica)", "Ethane/Propane/Butane"]
profiles.competitive_position: original Marcellus developer; top-tier well economics; Martica NGL complex adds diversification

profiles.business_description: Sherwin-Williams is a leading global manufacturer, distributor, and retailer of paint, coatings, and related products serving professional, industrial, commercial, and retail customers primarily in North and South America with additional operations in Europe, Asia, and Australia. The company operates through three segments—Paint Stores Group (company-operated specialty stores), Consumer Brands Group (branded/private-label products sold through third-party retailers), and Performance Coatings Group (industrial and specialty coatings sold globally)—generating $23.6 billion in revenue in 2025. From a creditor perspective, SHW carries ~$10.9 billion in total debt (net leverage ~2.4x EBITDA) and generates strong operating cash flow (~14.6% of net sales), though it faces ongoing environmental liabilities and lead paint litigation.

profiles.business_description: SM Energy Co. is a Permian and Uinta Basin E&P producing approximately 207 MBoe/d (53% oil) following the transformational $4.5B acquisition of Civitas/XCL Resources in 2024. The Midland Basin (Permian) provides proven, low-cost oil-weighted production, while the Uinta Basin in Utah adds high-API waxy crude that commands premium pricing ($2-4/bbl above WTI). SM has been one of the more aggressive mid-cap E&P acquirers, with the Civitas deal roughly doubling production and enterprise value. LTM revenue of $3.15B and EBITDA of $2.47B reflect the combined platform. The company is actively cleaning up the legacy Civitas debt stack through tenders and new issuance. The $5.0B RBL provides substantial liquidity headroom.
profiles.end_markets: ["Crude Oil Production", "Waxy Crude (Uinta)", "Natural Gas", "NGL Processing"]
profiles.competitive_position: dual-basin operator (Permian + Uinta); post-Civitas integration; Uinta premium crude

profiles.business_description: Summit Midstream Holdings LLC (NYSE: SMC) is a multi-basin gathering and processing midstream company operating natural gas and crude oil gathering systems across the Williston Basin (Bakken/North Dakota), DJ Basin (Colorado), Utica Shale (Ohio), Barnett Shale (North Texas), and Piceance Basin (Colorado). The company was restructured out of the original Summit Midstream Partners MLP. Revenue of $562M LTM across diversified but individually small G&P systems. The multi-basin footprint provides geographic diversification but lacks the scale advantages of single-basin specialists. Operations are fee-based under acreage dedication agreements with various E&P counterparties.

profiles.business_description: Sunoco LP is one of the largest independent fuel distributors in the United States, operating approximately 7,400 fuel distribution locations across 40+ states plus pipeline and terminal infrastructure. The MLP structure generates revenue from fuel distribution margins (wholesale-to-retail spread), pipeline tariffs, and terminal throughput fees. The 2024 NuStar acquisition added crude oil and refined product pipeline assets, while the 2025 Parkland Corporation deal expanded into Canadian fuel distribution. LTM revenue of $25.2B and EBITDA of $1.81B. SUN is the parent entity for NSUS (NuStar Logistics) bonds. The distribution coverage model is typical of fuel MLPs -- high leverage supported by stable, volume-driven cash flows with limited direct commodity price exposure.
profiles.end_markets: ["Fuel Distribution", "Pipeline & Terminal Operations", "Refined Product Storage"]
profiles.competitive_position: largest US independent fuel distributor; NuStar + Parkland integration

profiles.business_description: Stanley Black & Decker is a global manufacturer and marketer of hand tools, power tools, outdoor power equipment, and engineered fastening solutions with $15.1 billion in 2025 revenues. The company operates two segments: Tools & Outdoor (87% of revenue), anchored by DEWALT, CRAFTSMAN, and BLACK+DECKER brands, and Engineered Fastening (13%), serving automotive, industrial, and aerospace end markets. The company has undergone significant portfolio simplification via divestitures and completed a $2.1 billion cost reduction program, with proceeds from the pending CAM sale ($1.525-1.6B net) earmarked for debt reduction.

profiles.business_description: Synaptics is a fabless semiconductor designer delivering AI-enabled edge solutions covering touch, display, biometrics, wireless connectivity, audio/video processing and edge AI compute. Revenue of $1.07bn in FY2025 is split across three end-market categories with Core IoT (wireless) the fastest-growing segment (+53% YoY). The company operates asset-light through third-party wafer fabs (TSMC-ecosystem) and outsourced assembly/test, concentrating risk in a handful of Asian contract manufacturers. From a creditor standpoint, Synaptics carries meaningful intangible amortization drag (~$114mm/yr), recorded net losses in FY2025, and faces customer-concentration risk given dependence on a small number of OEM accounts.

profiles.business_description: Talos Energy Inc. is a Gulf of Mexico deepwater E&P producing approximately 89,000 boepd (~73% oil) from a portfolio of operated and non-operated properties in the shallow and deepwater GOM. The company materially increased scale through the $1.29B QuarterNorth Energy acquisition in early 2024, adding significant deepwater production and exploration inventory. Talos also operates a growing carbon capture and storage (CCS) business in the GOM, providing energy transition optionality similar to CRC. Revenue of $1.78B LTM and EBITDA of $822M. The capital structure uses 2nd-lien secured notes rather than the typical unsecured HY structure, reflecting GOM asset characteristics. The $700M RBL is first-lien with priority claim. Cash of $363M and $965M total liquidity provide a strong cushion for the cyclical GOM operating environment.

profiles.business_description: TriNet Group is the largest publicly traded Professional Employer Organization (PEO) focused on SMBs, processing $70B in payroll for ~323,200 worksite employees (WSEs) across technology, financial services, life sciences, nonprofit, and professional services verticals. The PEO model bundles HR, payroll, benefits, and compliance under TriNet as the employer of record; clients pay per-WSE fees that include a pass-through for insurance costs plus TriNet service margin. The insurance cost ratio (ICR) is the key EBITDA driver; when health cost trend exceeds re-pricing speed, margins compress sharply. TriNet repriced benefits rates in 2025, contributing to WSE attrition (-10% total WSEs YoY) but stabilizing ICR at 91%. Leverage is conservative at 1.7x net, with $500MM 3.5% Notes (2029) and $400MM 7.125% Notes (2031) representing a clean, investment-grade-aspirant capital structure for a business with strong cash generation.

Vertical integration is the core competitive strategy, though the company faces significant leverage, cyclical end-market exposure, and ongoing liquidity management challenges including a 60% dividend cut and new secured bond issuance in 2025.

profiles.business_description: TTM Technologies is a leading global manufacturer of advanced PCBs, mission systems, RF/microwave assemblies, and interconnect products, generating ~$2.9bn in FY2025 revenue across three segments: A&D (13 domestic facilities), Commercial (PCB fabrication in US, China, Malaysia, Canada), and RF&S Components (domestic + China RF). The company serves ~1,300 customers across aerospace/defense, data center computing, automotive, medical, and networking markets. From a credit perspective, TTMI benefits from a diversified end-market base with a growing share of high-margin A&D revenue, strong cash flow generation ($292mm operating cash flow in FY2025), and improving leverage profile. Capital intensity is elevated given the company's $240-260mm FY2026 capex guidance tied to new Syracuse (advanced US PCB) and Penang (Malaysia) facility buildouts.

The company operates across North America, Latin America, Europe, and Asia, with approximately $1.83 billion in net sales for FY2025. Titan's integrated wheel-and-tire manufacturing capability provides a competitive advantage, though the business is exposed to cyclical end markets, commodity input costs, and significant international operations.

profiles.business_description: Twilio is the leading Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS) provider, offering programmable messaging, voice, email, and video APIs plus customer data and engagement software (Segment CDP). As of December 2025, Twilio served 402,000+ Active Customer Accounts across enterprises and SMBs. FY25 revenue was $5.07B with usage-based pricing making it more macro-sensitive than pure subscription software. The company reorganized into a single operating segment in Q3 2025, simplifying reporting. Capital structure is conservative: $992M debt consisting of $500M 3.625% Senior Notes due 2029 and $500M 3.875% Senior Notes due 2031, with $682M cash -- net leverage of only 1.15x. Strong operating cash flow of $1.0B in FY25 provides significant coverage of fixed obligations. US carrier A2P messaging fee increases (June 2025 + Jan/Apr 2026) are pass-through -- gross margin % headwind.

profiles.business_description: Unisys is a global IT services company with three segments: Digital Workplace Solutions (DWS -- end-user computing, managed IT), Cloud Applications & Infrastructure (CA&I -- cloud migration, infrastructure modernization), and Enterprise Computing Solutions (ECS -- ClearPath Forward mainframe software and licenses). Revenue was $1.95B in 2025 (down 2.9% YoY) with GAAP net loss of $339.8M driven by $228M pension settlement losses and $55M goodwill impairment in DWS. ECS/ClearPath is the credit anchor: high-margin (~40% gross margin), sticky license renewals that generate the majority of gross profit in an otherwise thin-margin IT services business. The company refinanced in June 2025 via $700M 10.625% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 to retire the 6.875% 2027 notes -- extending maturity but nearly doubling the coupon, increasing annual interest expense by $21.5M to $53.4M.

profiles.business_description: United Rentals is the worlds largest equipment rental company, operating 1,768 locations across North America with a smaller presence in Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. The fleet carries $22.5B OEC across general construction, aerial work platforms, power/HVAC, trench safety, fluid solutions, and specialty categories. Revenue was $16.1B in 2025 (+5% YoY), with 86% from equipment rentals; fleet productivity improved 2.2% as time utilization, mix, and rates all contributed positively. Credit structure is asset-intensive: $15.9B of total debt is normal for this model, backed by the fleet and supported by 9.0x interest coverage. URI is the benchmark investment-grade-aspiring HY credit with massive scale, durable cash flows, and predictable capex cycle. Near-term risk: $1.577B due 2026 (AR securitization + ABL) and execution of the ongoing fleet cycle capex.

profiles.business_description: USA Compression Partners LP (NYSE: USAC) is one of the largest independent providers of contract natural gas compression services in the US, operating a fleet of compression equipment under multi-year contracts. The partnership serves E&P and midstream customers primarily in the Permian Basin, Eagle Ford Shale, and Mid-Continent. Revenue of $998M LTM. The MLP structure distributes cash flow to unitholders, requiring maintenance of distribution coverage above 1.0x. Energy Transfer (ET) is the general partner and majority owner, providing strategic alignment with the largest US midstream company. Fleet utilization consistently exceeds 90%.

profiles.business_description: Valaris Limited (NYSE: VAL) is a major offshore drilling contractor operating a fleet of jackup and floating rigs (drillships and semi-submersibles) serving IOCs, NOCs, and independent E&P companies globally. Valaris operates in key offshore basins including the Gulf of Mexico, Middle East, West Africa, North Sea, and Southeast Asia. Revenue of $2.37B LTM. The post-emergence fleet has been high-graded through selective reactivation of stacked rigs as day rates improve.

profiles.business_description: Viavi Solutions is a global provider of network test, monitoring and assurance solutions for telecom, cloud, enterprise, and defense markets, plus optical security/performance products (OSP) for anti-counterfeiting pigments, 3D sensing and automotive LiDAR. Revenue is split between NSE (Network & Service Enablement, ~82% of revenue) and OSP (~18%), with NSE showing strong growth in FY2025 driven by fiber/data center buildout demand, aerospace/defense expansion, and the January 2025 acquisition of Inertial Labs (PNT solutions, $121mm cash). From a credit standpoint, VIAV's balance sheet is distinguishably conservative: negative net debt (-$27mm as of June 2025) with $424mm cash against $396mm long-term debt and $246mm short-term debt (1.625% convertible notes maturing March 2026). The near-term maturity of the convertible notes is the primary credit event to monitor.
profiles.end_markets: ["Fiber/data center testing", "5G/6G wireless testing", "Aerospace & defense", "Anti-counterfeiting pigments", "3D sensing / automotive LiDAR", "Enterprise network monitoring", "Cloud service assurance"]

profiles.revenue_visibility: mid

profiles.business_description: Verra Mobility is a leading smart mobility technology provider offering toll/violations management (39% of revenue), title/registration services, automated traffic enforcement cameras, and commercial parking management. The company serves three segments: Commercial Services (~45% of revenue for tolling for Avis, Enterprise, Hertz, and FMC fleet customers), Government Solutions (~40% for photo enforcement contracts with municipalities, school districts, and law enforcement), and Parking Solutions (~15% for software and hardware for universities and healthcare facilities). Revenue is ~$966MM (2025), nearly entirely from recurring government and long-term commercial contracts. The NYCDOT contract renewal (effective January 2026, $998MM total value, 5-year term) is the landmark credit event. Net leverage of 2.5x and 5.8x interest coverage reflect a well-positioned, cash-generative credit with high visibility.
profiles.end_markets: Rental car companies, commercial fleets, municipalities, school districts, universities, healthcare facilities
profiles.geographic_mix: US ~80%, Australia ~10%, Europe ~8%, Canada ~2%; Government Solutions is international growth vector
profiles.customer_concentration: Moderate concentration: top 3 RACs (Avis, Enterprise, Hertz) represent significant portion of Commercial; NYCDOT single largest government client
profiles.commodity_exposure: Minimal; camera hardware and software; some exposure to electronic components for enforcement hardware
profiles.capex_intensity: Low-to-moderate; asset-light software model augmented by government hardware installation for photo enforcement
profiles.business_cyclicality: Low; government contracts and tolling revenue are volume-based but highly sticky; recession-resilient
profiles.competitive_position: Dominant in US commercial fleet tolling (relationships with all three major RACs); established in government photo enforcement. Switching costs are extremely high - VRRM is embedded in government IT systems and client workflows.
profiles.revenue_visibility: Very high; ~85%+ recurring from multi-year government contracts and long-term RAC/fleet relationships

profiles.business_description: Bristow Group Inc. (NYSE: VTOL) is the world's largest provider of offshore aviation services, operating a fleet of approximately 225 helicopters serving offshore oil and gas platforms, government search-and-rescue (SAR) operations, and other transportation missions. Key SAR contracts include the UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency, Ireland, and Norway. Revenue of $1.49B LTM. Bristow emerged from Chapter 11 in 2019 and has since rebuilt into a BB-rated credit. The Jan 2026 $500M secured notes are collateralized by ~119 aircraft. The fleet serves all major offshore basins globally.

profiles.business_description: Valvoline Inc. is a pure-play automotive preventive maintenance retailer operating and franchising approximately 2,400 service center locations across the U.S. and Canada under the VIOC, GCOC, and Oil Changers brands. profiles.business_description: NCR Voyix is a global unified-commerce platform provider focused on retail (point-of-sale, self-checkout software) and restaurant (POS, order management) verticals, serving ~13,500 employees across ~30 countries. The company is a post-spin (October 2023) and post-Digital Banking divestiture (September 2024, $2.45bn proceeds) entity; it completed the Hardware Business Transition (outsourcing self-checkout/POS hardware manufacturing to Ennoconn) in 2024. FY2025 revenue was $2.7bn (-5% YoY) but recurring revenue (software + services) grew 3% to 62% of total; Adjusted EBITDA of $425mm (+22% YoY) reflects ongoing mix shift to software/SaaS. From a credit perspective, VYX carries $1.1bn of senior notes with net leverage of ~3.1x and tight liquidity ($231mm cash, $500mm revolver), making the free cash flow conversion trajectory and covenant headroom the primary monitoring metrics.

profiles.business_description: Wabtec Corporation is a global provider of technology-based locomotives, equipment, systems, and services for the freight rail and passenger transit industries, as well as mining, marine, and industrial markets. The company operates through two segments—Freight (~72% of revenue) and Transit (~28%)—with approximately 60% of total net sales derived from aftermarket parts and services, providing meaningful revenue stability. With a $27.4 billion backlog and an installed base of nearly 24,600 locomotives, Wabtec benefits from significant recurring revenue streams and high switching costs.

profiles.business_description: WBI Operations LLC is a regulated natural gas transmission pipeline and underground storage subsidiary of MDU Resources Group, Inc. (NYSE: MDU). The company operates approximately 3,700 miles of natural gas pipeline and storage facilities across Montana, Wyoming, North Dakota, and South Dakota. Revenue is derived from FERC-regulated transportation tariffs and storage fees. WBI was originally listed as OFS but is correctly classified as Gas Distribution -- it is a regulated pipeline utility, not an oilfield services company. MDU Resources provides a parent guarantee on the PGIM private shelf debt.

profiles.business_description: WESCO International is a leading B2B distributor of electrical, communications, and utility products operating 700+ sites in ~50 countries with ~21,000 employees and $20B+ in annual revenues. Created by the 2020 merger of WESCO and Anixter, the company operates through three strategic business units: Electrical and Electronic Solutions (EES for construction/industrial/OEM), Communications and Security Solutions (CSS for data center/AV/security), and Utility and Broadband Solutions (UBS for electric/gas utilities and broadband). The combined entity is the #1 or #2 North American distributor in each segment and serves 130,000 customers via 35,000 supplier relationships. Credit relevance: $5.8B debt at 4.0x net leverage reflects Anixter acquisition leverage that management is steadily reducing; near-term maturity is manageable ($25MM due 2026), but $1.325B 7.25% notes mature in 2028 representing the most significant refinancing event.

profiles.business_description: Westlake Corporation is a vertically integrated global manufacturer of housing and infrastructure products (HIP) and performance and essential materials (PEM), operating across two principal segments. The company is highly integrated along its materials chain from ethylene and chlor-alkali into vinyls, polyethylene, and epoxy, with significant downstream integration into PVC-based building products, pipe, and compounds. As one of the largest global chlorovinyls producers, Westlake's credit profile is exposed to commodity chemical cyclicality in PEM while benefiting from more stable, construction-driven cash flows in HIP.

profiles.business_description: W&T Offshore, Inc. is a small Gulf of Mexico shelf E&P operating mature, shallow-water oil and gas properties primarily on the GOM continental shelf and deepwater. The company has a long operating history dating back to 1983 and specializes in extending the productive life of acquired mature properties through workovers, recompletions, and development drilling. Revenue of $501M LTM and EBITDA of $68M reflect the thin margins of a mature-asset operator. W&T's GOM shelf position carries unique risks including hurricane exposure, high operating costs, and significant plugging and abandonment (P&A) liabilities. The Jan 2025 refinancing simplified the capital structure to a single $350M 2nd-lien note.
profiles.end_markets: ["Crude Oil Production", "Natural Gas", "Mature GOM Field Development"]
profiles.geographic_mix: US 100% (Gulf of Mexico - continental shelf and deepwater)
profiles.competitive_position: small GOM shelf specialist; mature asset operator; high P&A liability exposure

profiles.business_description: TeraWulf is a vertically integrated owner, developer, and operator of large-scale digital infrastructure in the US, pivoting from Bitcoin mining to high-performance computing (HPC) data centers for AI/ML workloads. The company controls two primary campuses: Lake Mariner Data Campus (Barker, NY; 245 MW legacy mining + 18 MW HPC as of Dec 2025) and Abernathy HPC Campus (Texas; 168 MW, 100% pre-leased to Fluidstack with Google credit enhancement, 25-year sublease). Total contracted HPC capacity is 522 MW across both campuses. The capital structure is unusual: $3.54B gross debt comprising ~$850M in convertible notes (2030, 2031, 2032 converts) and a $3.3B+ fair value 2030 Secured Notes position -- DB total debt appears to include non-cash/fair value adjustments. Going concern risk was previously flagged but HPC contracts with Google credit-enhanced counterparties have improved the credit outlook materially.

profiles.business_description: Xerox is a workplace technology company delivering document management, IT infrastructure, and managed services to enterprise customers globally, with FY2025 total revenue of $7.0bn. The company completed the transformative Lexmark acquisition (July 1, 2025) and ITsavvy acquisition (Nov 2024), expanding into the A4 color printing segment and IT infrastructure solutions respectively. Segments are Print & Other and IT Solutions; legacy Xerox revenue declined 7.6% on a pro forma basis in FY2025, offset by acquisition contributions. From a creditor perspective, XRX is a deeply distressed credit: reported net losses of $1.03bn in FY2025 (vs $1.32bn in FY2024), negative EBITDA of -$157mm on a reported basis, gross debt of $4.25bn against only $512mm of cash, and a $3.3bn accumulated AOCI deficit from pension obligations. The company funded Lexmark via high-cost secured notes (10.25% First Lien, 13.50% Second Lien) that materially increase the interest burden on an already cash-strained business.

profiles.business_description: Ziff Davis is a vertically focused digital media and internet company with five reportable segments: Technology & Shopping ($357M revenue), Gaming & Entertainment ($184M), Health & Wellness ($402M), Connectivity ($231M), and Cybersecurity & Martech ($278M). Total FY25 revenue was $1.45B. The company is a serial acquirer -- deploying $3.3B across ~100 acquisitions since 2012 -- with a systematic M&A process targeting free-cash-flow-generative digital businesses. Capital structure includes $457M 4.625% Senior Notes (due 2030), $149M 1.75% Convertible Notes, $260M 3.625% Convertible Notes, and a $350M revolving credit facility ($349M available). Net leverage is low at 0.32x on ~$341M EBITDA with $607M cash. The Cybersecurity & Martech segment faces structural headwinds with revenue declining from $291M (2023) to $278M (2025).

profiles.business_description: ZipRecruiter is a two-sided AI-powered online job marketplace connecting employers and job seekers, monetizing primarily through employer subscription and pay-per-click job posting fees. The platform generates substantially all revenue from employers (flat-rate subscriptions or CPC performance pricing), while the job seeker side is free. Revenue was $449MM in 2025 (-5% vs. $474MM in 2024), reflecting continued softness in hiring activity across the technology and knowledge-work verticals most served by the platform. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $41MM (from $78MM in 2024), making this a thin-margin digital marketplace with extreme operating leverage in both directions. Credit relevance: $545MM of total debt (9.8x gross leverage on $56MM LTM EBITDA) is carried in $550MM of 2030 senior unsecured notes plus $230MM 1.5% convertible notes; the revolving credit facility is fully undrawn. The extreme leverage is a function of a small EBITDA denominator, not absolute debt size; the company has $188MM cash.
profiles.end_markets: SMB and enterprise employers across all industries; job seekers; concentration in tech, professional services, and white-collar roles
profiles.geographic_mix: Predominantly US (~95%); small and growing international presence; foreign currency exposure in Canada, UK, Israel (personnel costs)

profiles.commodity_exposure: None; pure digital marketplace; cost structure is personnel (engineering, sales, G&A) and marketing spend

profiles.competitive_position: Rated #1 job site in the US by user satisfaction; competes with Indeed (dominant), LinkedIn (professional), and Monster/CareerBuilder. AI matching and proactive candidate outreach differentiate; network effects create some defensibility. Scale disadvantage vs. Indeed.
profiles.revenue_visibility: Low; primarily subscription and CPC from employers; churn and hiring market cycles create significant revenue volatility

profiles.business_description: ZoomInfo is a global leader in B2B go-to-market intelligence software, providing AI-powered sales, marketing, operations, and recruiting data/workflows to 35,000+ customers. Revenue was $1.25B in FY25 (+2.9% YoY), with subscriptions representing substantially all revenue. The platform consists of three layers: Intelligence (data on companies/contacts), Orchestration (routing/enrichment), and Engagement (multi-channel outreach). The company originated as a PE-backed LBO (Henry Schuck/TA Associates/Carlyle/etc.) and went public in 2020; PE-originated leverage remains in the capital structure ($1.32B total debt: First Lien TL $579M at SOFR+1.75%, Senior Notes 3.875% 2029 at $644M, revolver). Net leverage of 3.63x is the primary credit overhang. Non-GAAP Adjusted Operating Income was $446M in FY25 (36% margin) showing strong underlying cash generation capacity.

profiles.business_description: Aramark is a leading global provider of food and facilities management services, generating $18.5B in fiscal 2025 revenue across two reportable segments: FSS United States ($13.2B, 71%) and FSS International ($5.3B, 29% across 15 countries). ARMK holds top-2 North America and top-3 international positions in food/facilities, with institutional clients providing a captive customer base. Sysco distributes ~43% of US/Canada food purchases.

profiles.business_description: Infinity Natural Resources LLC is an Appalachian natural gas E&P focused on the Utica and Marcellus Shales in Ohio, West Virginia, and Pennsylvania. The company IPO'd on NYSE in January 2025 under ticker INR, establishing public equity market access. Infinity has grown rapidly through the $350M acquisition of Antero Resources' Ohio Utica acreage, nearly doubling its production base. 2026 guidance of 345-375 MMcfe/d represents ~70% YoY growth. The company operates in one of the lowest-cost US gas basins, with Appalachian breakevens providing structural cost advantage vs Haynesville peers. Capital expenditure of $430M+ annually reflects the aggressive drilling program to build scale.
profiles.end_markets: ["Natural Gas Production", "NGL Processing", "Appalachian Shale Development"]
profiles.competitive_position: growing Appalachian operator; IPO'd Jan 2025; low-cost basin

profiles.business_description: Resideo Technologies is a global manufacturer and distributor of home comfort, safety, and security products, spun off from Honeywell in 2018. The company operates through two segments: Products and Solutions (HVAC controls, smoke/CO detection, security products under Honeywell Home, BRK, First Alert brands) and ADI Global Distribution (specialty low-voltage product distribution to 100K+ professional installers). In July 2025, Resideo announced an intent to spin off ADI Global Distribution as an independent public company via tax-free distribution, fundamentally restructuring the credit profile. Revenue was $7.47B in 2025 (+10.5%), driven largely by ADI scale; post-spin the remaining Products and Solutions entity will be meaningfully smaller. The Honeywell indemnification obligation was terminated via the August 2025 term loan refinancing that funded ~$1.2B, resolving the defining legacy credit overhang.
profiles.end_markets: Residential and commercial HVAC, home security, fire detection/suppression, professional installer channel
profiles.geographic_mix: US ~55%, Europe ~25%, Rest of world ~20%; global footprint supports residential/commercial end markets
profiles.customer_concentration: ADI serves 100K+ professional contractors; Products and Solutions has broad OEM and channel exposure
profiles.commodity_exposure: Moderate; electronic components, copper, plastics; some pass-through capability in distribution
profiles.capex_intensity: Low; manufacturing is outsourced for most products; ADI is asset-light distributor
profiles.business_cyclicality: Mid; residential end markets cycle with housing; commercial is more stable; HVAC replacement is repair-driven
profiles.competitive_position: Leading positions in HVAC controls and home safety/detection. ADI is a top-3 specialty low-voltage distributor globally. Honeywell Home brand strength provides pricing power in professional channel despite premium positioning.
profiles.revenue_visibility: Moderate; ADI is transactional distribution; Products and Solutions has recurring aftermarket/replacement demand

profiles.business_description: Venture Global LNG Inc is the parent holding company and development entity for the Venture Global LNG platform, one of the largest LNG development programs in North America. The platform includes: Calcasieu Pass (10 mtpa, Cameron Parish, LA -- operational, bonded as VENTGL), Plaquemines LNG (~20 mtpa, Plaquemines Parish, LA -- under construction, bonded as VEGLPL), and the proposed CP2 project (~20 mtpa, Cameron Parish). VG IPO'd in January 2025 on NYSE, raising $1.75B. The company uses a modular mid-scale liquefaction technology that differentiates it from traditional large-train LNG developers. Combined capacity of 50+ mtpa would make VG one of the largest LNG companies globally.
profiles.end_markets: ["LNG Development", "LNG Export Operations", "Natural Gas Procurement", "Project Finance"]
profiles.geographic_mix: US (Louisiana Gulf Coast -- Cameron Parish + Plaquemines Parish)
profiles.competitive_position: one of largest LNG development platforms globally; IPO'd Jan 2025; 50+ mtpa combined capacity

profiles.business_description: Zebra Technologies is the global leader in Automatic Identification and Data Capture (AIDC), manufacturing mobile computers, barcode scanners, RFID readers, thermal printers, RTLS systems, and related software/services. FY2025 net sales were $5,396mm (+8.3% YoY) with 10,700 employees across 129 facilities, selling in 179 countries through 10,000+ channel partners. The company realigned its reporting segments in Q4 2025 to Connected Frontline (CF; mobile computing, POS, self-service) and Asset Visibility & Automation (AVA; thermal printing, RFID, machine vision). From a creditor standpoint, ZBRA's credit profile is well-supported by strong OCF ($1.0bn+ range), market leadership, and diversified end-markets, offset by 2.2x net leverage, a front-loaded maturity schedule ($141mm due 2026, $1.87bn due 2027), and an active share repurchase program that consumed $587mm of FCF in FY2025.

profiles.business_description: Gen Digital (formerly NortonLifeLock) is the consumer cybersafety company, operating the Norton, Avast, LifeLock, and related brands serving ~500M users in 150+ countries. Products span antivirus/security, privacy (VPN), identity theft protection, and financial wellness (MoneyLion acquisition). Revenue is primarily direct subscription (~$3.5B annually). Post-Avast merger ($8.6B, 2022) the company carries $7.97B of debt (3.2x net leverage) with Term A/B facilities and senior notes. Management is executing on deleveraging ($370MM net debt reduction in FY2025) and shareholder returns ($955MM returned in FY2025).

profiles.business_description: NGL Energy Operating LLC is a diversified midstream MLP operating three primary segments: water solutions (produced water gathering, transportation, disposal, and recycling in the Permian Basin and Bakken), crude oil logistics (purchasing, transporting, and reselling crude oil), and NGL marketing. The water solutions business is the strategic core and primary EBITDA growth driver, benefiting from increasing produced water volumes as Permian Basin operators drill deeper and wider-spacing wells. Revenue of $3.18B LTM. NGL was a deeply distressed credit in 2020-2021 (CCC-rated) but has rebuilt through the water business pivot and Feb 2024 $2.9B refinancing.
profiles.end_markets: ["Produced Water Disposal", "Crude Oil Logistics", "NGL Marketing & Distribution"]
profiles.competitive_position: water solutions leader in Permian; rebuilt from CCC distress; secured capital structure

profiles.business_description: Borealis Foods is a U.S.-based integrated food science and manufacturing company focused on affordable nutrition, producing ramen noodle products under brands including Chef Woo, Chef Ramsay, Ramen Express, and Woodles. Revenue is highly discretionary and cyclical, dependent on consumer confidence, interest rates, and dealer floor plan financing conditions.

profiles.business_description: Ciena is a leading network technology company providing optical networking hardware, software, and services to cloud providers, service providers, and enterprises. Revenue reached $4.8B in FY2025 (+19% YoY) driven by AI-driven bandwidth demand, with cloud providers now ~30%+ of revenue. The company's proprietary WaveLogic coherent modem technology underpins its competitive advantage in high-capacity optical transport. Segments: Networking Platforms (77% of revenue, led by Optical Networking), Platform Software and Services (8%), Blue Planet Automation Software (2%), and Global Services (13%). Backlog grew from $2.1B to $5.0B, signaling strong forward demand from AI infrastructure buildouts.

profiles.business_description: CrowdStrike is the leading AI-native cybersecurity platform company, offering 33 cloud modules via SaaS subscription. ARR reached $5.25B as of Jan 31, 2026 (+24% YoY), with subscription revenue of $4.56B in fiscal 2026. The Falcon platform is delivered via a single lightweight sensor and cloud-scale AI, serving enterprise endpoints, cloud workloads, identities, and SIEM. Dollar-based NRR remained strong. From a credit perspective, CrowdStrike has $745MM of 3.00% Senior Notes due Feb 2029, offset by $5.2B cash and strong subscription FCF generation, making it effectively investment-grade quality despite GAAP losses from heavy S&M investment.

profiles.business_description: Columbus McKinnon Corporation is a leading designer, manufacturer, and marketer of intelligent motion solutions for material handling, with key products including hoists, crane components, precision conveyor systems, rigging tools, actuators, and digital power/motion control systems sold primarily through industrial distributors. The company serves diverse end markets including manufacturing, energy, transportation, life sciences, food & beverage, and e-commerce, with approximately 57% U.S. and 43% international revenue. In February 2026, CMCO closed the transformative Kito Crosby acquisition funded by ~$3.05B in committed debt and $800M in convertible preferred equity from CD&R, materially increasing leverage and significantly expanding its lifting, securement, and consumables portfolio.

profiles.business_description: Elastic N.V. is the Search AI Company, providing the Elasticsearch platform for search, observability, and security use cases. Products are available as Elastic Cloud (multi-cloud SaaS) and self-managed on-prem. The three solutions — Elasticsearch, Elastic Observability, and Elastic Security — all run on one platform. Revenue is subscription-driven with cloud revenue growing faster than self-managed. From a credit perspective, Elastic carries $570MM of 4.125% Senior Notes due July 2029, with $728MM cash providing a net cash position, though low EBITDA ($76MM LTM) means debt is high relative to earnings.

The Delaware Basin land position is the collateral -- 300k+ acres of surface rights that are essential for Permian development. Revenue grows with drilling activity without requiring LandBridge capex. Water sourcing (~25% of revenue) is a secular growth business as Permian water volumes increase. Key watches: Permian drilling activity levels, surface use agreement pricing power, water sourcing growth trajectory, and any large land acquisitions that could add leverage.

transcript_signals.credit_relevant_summary: Enerflex's Dec 2025 refinancing was a clear credit upgrade: retired the 9.0% secured 2027 notes and replaced with $400M 6.875% unsecured 2031 notes -- lower coupon, longer maturity, and release of collateral (secured -> unsecured). This transition typically signals BB-/BB-level credit improvement. Aftermarket services (~20% revenue) provide a recurring revenue base that reduces cyclicality. FMP data is CAD-denominated, creating apparent data distortion in USD analysis. Global diversification (Canada/US/ME/LatAm) reduces geographic concentration. Key watches: international project pipeline, aftermarket revenue growth, and leverage trajectory in USD terms.

transcript_signals.credit_relevant_summary: Bristow's Jan 2026 refinancing extended maturity from 2028 to 2033 while reducing coupon from 6.875% to 6.75% -- a clear credit improvement despite the modest coupon change. The 1st-lien security backed by ~119 aircraft provides strong collateral. At 2.7x leverage and 5.8x interest coverage, the credit profile is solid for an asset-intensive aviation business. Government SAR contracts (~25% revenue) provide a counter-cyclical revenue floor that differentiates Bristow from pure offshore service companies. LTM FCF of $56M is modest given $232M EBITDA -- aircraft maintenance and fleet renewal absorb significant cash. Key watches: SAR contract renewals (UK/Norway), offshore platform count driving helicopter demand, fleet age and maintenance capex, and helicopter market supply-demand balance.

transcript_signals.credit_relevant_summary: ASGN's filing reflects a business at a strategic transition — shifting from its staffing heritage toward higher-value IT consulting while simultaneously rebranding the entire enterprise to Everforth. The Federal Government $2.9B backlog is the credit's most important stabilizer, providing multi-year revenue visibility against commercial softness. The 2.7x interest coverage is thin for IT staffing's earnings volatility, but the 1.49x senior secured leverage vs. 3.75x covenant leaves substantial room before covenant violation. The Everforth rebrand, while strategically sound, creates near-term transition risk in government contracting where past performance certifications are name-specific.
