coverage_memos.memo_md:
MH — McGraw Hill, Inc.
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: initiation
Quarters covered: FY2026 Q1-Q3 (period ending Dec 31, 2025; bond co-issuer MHED also references this credit; Q4 FY2026 prints ~early June)
Date: 2026-05-01

I. SNAPSHOT

McGraw Hill is the second-largest US K-12 and Higher Education publisher (after Pearson and tied with Cengage), re-IPO'd June 2025 from Platinum Equity ownership at CIK 1951070. Three reportable segments: Higher Education (the recurring digital growth engine — Connect, ALEKS, Evergreen platform), K-12 (textbook adoption cycles, larger/lumpier), Global Professional & International (smaller). Bond co-issuer remains the legacy MHED (McGraw-Hill Education, Inc., CIK 1651444) — same credit, two SEC reporting entities for historical bond-indenture reasons. The credit lens here applies G.W.'s media framework: recurring digital subscriber economics × content cash-vs-accrual gap × post-IPO deleveraging trajectory. ML L4: Services / Printing & Publishing (legacy Bloomberg/ICE classification — but the business is 84% digital recurring, not print-cycle). Q3 fiscal 2026 (printed 2026-02-11; period ending Dec 31, 2025) was a beat with raised FY guide — adj EBITDA $136M (+7.7% YoY at 31.3% margin), revenue $434M (+4.2%), recurring revenue +14.8% to 82% of total. Net leverage 2.9x at Q3 end, mgmt target 2.0-2.5x. Equity is bearish despite the operational strength — sustained_decline flag, $11.98 close at 17.7% of 52w range, post-IPO drift.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE

- Total debt: ~$2.61B at Q3 fiscal 2026 (Dec 31, 2025) per XBRL
- Cash $514M; net debt ~$2.10B
- LTM adj EBITDA $700M+ (FY2026 guide $729-739M; Q3 alone $136M, Q2 alone ~$220M, Q1 alone ~$95M based on segment cadence)
- Net leverage 2.9x (mgmt-cited Q3 end); target 2.0-2.5x
- Critical content-amortization gap (G.W.'s primary watch): GAAP D&A is enormous because textbook content development costs are capitalized and amortized over multi-year title lifecycles. Q3 GAAP D&A $276M on $434M revenue = 64% of revenue. Adj EBITDA $136M strips this out. The cash-vs-accrual question is whether content investment cash spend matches the amortization — capex guide is 8-9% of revenue ($170-190M FY 2026), versus implied content amortization run-rate $1.0-1.1B annually (D&A annualizes from quarterly numbers). The accrual gap is favorable here — they're running off prior-period content investment. That's the cycle inflection of a stable digital publisher.
- Tranche stack (per call): primary tranche is a Term Loan B (size not disclosed in transcript but implied from context); revolving credit facility undrawn at Q3; legacy McGraw-Hill Education senior notes outstanding at the MHED entity
- IPO proceeds $392.9M used for term loan paydown
- YTD term loan prepayments: $596M (organic cash-driven, not refi); $200M Q3 alone, $50M expected Q4 — annualized interest savings $41M
- Liquidity: $514M cash + undrawn revolver = $964M total
- Refi wall: not in transcript; legacy MHED senior notes likely 2027-2029 vintage and may sit at 6-7% coupons that refi at lower current rates given the deleveraging trajectory
- Capital allocation explicit: "prioritize reinvestment and debt reduction"; no buybacks, no dividends, "bolt-on tuck-in" M&A only

III. THESIS

The thesis is a credit-positive deleveraging story driven by recurring digital revenue and content-amortization tailwind. McGraw Hill prints what G.W.'s framework rewards in media: 84% digital revenue, 82% recurring revenue, with recurring growing +14.8% YoY in Q3 — these aren't streaming subs but they're functionally identical (instructor adoption + student access codes + multi-year district contracts). Higher Education is the engine: +24% revenue growth, +33.5% recurring growth, 30% market share (record), Evergreen platform now 70% of segment revenue. The Q3 transcript is full of AI integration commentary — AI Reader (1M users, 16M Q3 learning interactions), Sharpen Advantage (1M users in 9 months, institutional license rather than per-professor), ALEKS for Calculus (~$100M TAM addition). The cycle position is favorable: K-12 contracted -14.6% in Q3 (anticipated, smaller adoption cycle year — 2026 should rebound on Texas / Florida adoption opening), and the company guided to that contraction. The credit math is clean: 2.9x net leverage moving toward 2.5x via $250M+ of FCF generation per quarter (operating cash flow $309M Q3, +12% YoY) while management explicitly directs cash to debt paydown. The MHED legacy senior notes likely refi at lower coupons in 2027-2028 as leverage clears 2.5x and the post-IPO public-company status improves credit pricing. G.W.'s typical concern — content cash spend masking accrual — is INVERTED here: capex guide 8-9% of revenue ($170-190M) is below current D&A run-rate ($1.0B+ annualized GAAP), meaning the existing content base is amortizing faster than they're reinvesting. That's structurally favorable to FCF until/unless content underinvestment shows up in market-share losses (no evidence yet — share at record 30%). The bearish equity tape — sustained_decline flag, 17.7% of 52w range — reflects post-IPO float overhang and PE sell-down concerns, not credit deterioration.

IV. KEY RISKS

- K-12 adoption cycle dependency. Q3 K-12 -14.6% is "anticipated" but the segment is highly cyclical — California, Texas, and Florida adoption windows drive 60%+ of K-12 revenue in any given year. A delay in 2026 Texas adoption would push EBITDA recovery to 2027.
- Content underinvestment risk. Capex 8-9% of revenue might be too low — the cash-vs-accrual gap is favorable today, but if titles age out without replacement spend, market share erodes 2-3 years later. Watch the 30% MPI share for any deterioration.
- AI substitution risk. Generative AI (ChatGPT, Claude) tutors compete with adaptive learning platforms (ALEKS, Sharpen). McGraw Hill is positioning as AI-enabled (Morning Consult ranked them #1 educator-trusted AI brand), but the long-tail substitution risk is real — institutional licensing is the moat.
- Platinum Equity sell-down overhang. Post-IPO PE retains stake; secondary offerings could pressure equity (which doesn't directly hit credit) but signals a near-term capital allocation question.
- Refi pricing risk on legacy MHED notes. 2027-2029 refi window; current 5-7% coupon paper refis at higher rates than expected if HY market widens. $500M-$1B of notes affected.
- Higher Education growth deceleration. +24% Q3 segment growth is hot; deceleration to single-digits in 2027-2028 would compress the overall recurring-revenue growth from +14.8% to 5-7%, slowing FCF and the deleveraging trajectory.
- Tariff/import risk on physical print. K-12 still has print component; paper input costs and logistics expose the segment to commodity tape.

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Q3 fiscal 2026 (printed 2026-02-11; period ending Dec 31, 2025): revenue $434M (+4.2% YoY), adj EBITDA $136M (+7.7%, 31.3% margin +100bps), gross margin 85.3% (+100bps), recurring revenue $357M (+14.8%, 82% of total), digital revenue $364M (+11%, 84% of total), operating cash flow $309M (+12%). Higher Ed +24% YoY ($225M); K-12 -14.6% (anticipated cycle); Professional +2%; International -1.8%. Q3 term loan prepayment $200M; YTD $596M; expected Q4 $50M+. FY 2026 guide raised: revenue $2.067-2.087B, adj EBITDA $729-739M; capex 8-9% of revenue. AI metrics: AI Reader 1M users (16M Q3 interactions); Sharpen Advantage 1M users in 9 months. CFO Sallmann: "We remain committed to a net leverage target of 2 to 2.5x and pursuing strategic tuck-in M&A." Equity composite N/A (no peer group set) in pipeline, but tape is decisively bearish: $11.98 close, 52w range $10.70-$18.00 (17.7% of range — near the IPO-low), 5d -7.74%, 20d -12.71%, sustained_decline flag triggered today (-12.7% over 20d). 90d realized vol 45.8%. Fundamental composite N/A — model hasn't run for this name yet given the just-onboarded data layer.

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- Q4 fiscal 2026 print (~early June 2026): adj EBITDA at top of $729-739M FY guide range = thesis intact; below midpoint suggests Higher Ed deceleration
- Net leverage at Q4 fiscal print: <2.7x = on track to hit 2.5x target by mid-FY 2027; >3.0x = deleveraging stalled
- K-12 segment Q1 fiscal 2027 (period ending June 30, 2026) — first read on whether the 2026 Texas adoption is delivering; flat-to-up YoY = cycle bottom confirmed
- Higher Ed segment growth — deceleration below +15% YoY signals cycle peak; below +10% = institutional license mix not extending the runway
- Term loan paydown cadence: $40M+/quarter through FY 2027 keeps the leverage walk on schedule
- Any 8-K announcing tender, exchange offer, or refi on MHED legacy senior notes — likely event in 2027 once leverage clears 2.5x
- Platinum Equity ownership disclosure — secondary offering or block sale shifts equity supply but is a credit-neutral overhang
- Revolver utilization > 0% (currently undrawn; first draw signals working capital seasonality reversal — Q4/Q1 is normally cash trough)
- Capex run-rate trajectory — 8-9% of revenue is the floor; if capex drops below 7%, content underinvestment risk grows
- Market share (MPI) data quarterly — drop below 28% from current 30% record signals competitive pressure (Pearson, Cengage, Wiley moves)
- Any AI-tutoring partnership or competitor disclosure (OpenAI, Anthropic education offerings) — institutional-license value test

Sign: — G.W.

NXST — Nexstar Media Inc.
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: refresh (v2 — Q1 2026 10-Q + 5/7 earnings call)
Quarters covered: 2024-Q2 to 2026-Q1
Date: 2026-05-11

I. SNAPSHOT
The post-TEGNA dominant US broadcaster. Closed TEGNA 3/19/2026 with FCC waiver to the 39% cap; pro forma 265 stations, 132 of 210 DMAs, 54.5% US household reach net of UHF discount. Q1 2026 print includes only 13 days of TEGNA contribution. The DirecTV-led antitrust suit has produced a **court-mandated hold-separate** under which TEGNA operates as a distinct Nexstar subsidiary — operational integration is blocked pending litigation resolution. Media / Media Content. The credit lens is broadcaster-classical (net retrans, political-cycle EBITDA flex, M&A execution) plus a binary legal-process variable on top.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE (Q1 2026 / 3/31/26 from 10-Q + earnings call)
- Total debt: **$12.42B** ($12.15B LT + $274M current) — jumped from $6.44B at 12/31/25 on TEGNA close.

III. THESIS
Q1 2026 was a strong standalone print — revenue $1.40B (+13.1% YoY), adj EBITDA $470M (+$89M; TEGNA contributed $31M of the YoY add), adj FCF $420M (legacy Nexstar $400M). NewsNation primetime viewers +85% YoY in March. The Q1 result demonstrates the standalone earnings engine is intact. The credit overhang is the litigation — three concurrent proceedings (9th Circuit appeal of preliminary injunction, US District Court trial in ED California, DC Circuit challenge to the FCC approval). Beth Wilkinson is lead trial/appellate counsel. Management has guided "limited" forward guidance through the litigation. The court denied DirecTV's emergency stay request — a small positive procedural read. Net leverage at 3.84x is well below the 4.75x covenant; covenant cushion is real. Bond investors should price the litigation as a 6-12 month duration event, not a permanent integration block; the synergies remain achievable per management ("if and when we get this resolved, we will be executing on our plan as we had originally intended").

IV. KEY RISKS
- Litigation duration — every quarter of hold-separate is a quarter without operational integration. Synergy realization is a 2027 story at the earliest. If court orders divestitures (rather than just delays), pro forma EBITDA assumptions for the credit re-rate.

Six consecutive trend-divergence flags in early May (5/2-5/7) at -2.5% to -2.8% over 5d vs TMT median +0.5% to +1.1% — read as litigation-overhang chop, not fundamentals weakness. 90d realized vol 47% (53rd percentile, normal). **Fundamental score v2 upgraded from 3.9 yellow to 5.2 yellow** on Q1 data — buckets: leverage 2.5 (slightly up from 2.1), market_risk 8.2 (up from 5.7 — biggest single-bucket move; the model is reading the cap-structure post-TEGNA more favorably than the bond market is currently), cash_flow 4.8 (up from 4.3), profitability 8.1 (up from 4.5 — the strong Q1 print flowed through), default_risk 6.2 (up from 5.0). coverage_memos.memo_md:
PARA — Paramount Skydance Corp (bonds at Paramount Global subsidiary)
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: initiation
Quarters covered: 2024-Q1 to 2025-Q4 (Q4 2025 / FY 2025 print 2026-02-25; Skydance merger closed 2025-08-07; pending WBD acquisition close Q3 2026)
Date: 2026-05-01

I. SNAPSHOT

Paramount Skydance Corp (NASDAQ: PSKY) is the post-2025 merged entity combining the legacy Paramount Global (Viacom-CBS) with Skydance Media — closed August 7, 2025. The franchise spans CBS broadcast network + Paramount Pictures studio + Paramount+ streaming + MTV/Comedy Central/Nickelodeon cable + CBS local stations + Pluto TV (free ad-supported). The credit lens here is the G.W. media-content playbook applied to a post-merger media holdco: subscriber economics (Paramount+ + linear) × content amortization (CBS sports rights + Paramount studio output) × leverage capacity (post-merger structure + WBD financing complexity). ML L4: Media / Media Content. The bonds remain at the Paramount Global subsidiary level (legacy CIK 813828) — bondholders retain claims on the operating subsidiary, not the new public parent. Two defining events: (1) Skydance merger closed Aug 7, 2025 with $4.45B cash to Paramount Class A shareholders + Skydance equity contribution; (2) pending Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition at $110.9B EV ($31/share to WBD shareholders), shareholder-approved April 23, 2026, expected close Q3 2026 — financed in part by $24B pledge from Gulf sovereign wealth funds (PSKY filing FCC for foreign ownership approval). FY 2025 revenue $28.89B, adj EBITDA $3.8B; 2026 guide revenue $30B (+4%), adj EBITDA $3.8B. Equity composite bullish: $11.09 close (20.2% of 52w range), 1m +16.49% — pricing WBD deal close.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE

- Total debt ~$14-15B at Paramount Global subsidiary level (per typical pre-merger structure; specific Q3 2025 XBRL detail limited because data only spans the post-merger period from Aug 7, 2025)
- Cash $3.26B at Q3 2025 (post-merger first quarter)
- Tranche stack (per legacy Paramount Global structure):
  - Senior unsecured notes at Paramount Global (multiple tranches, coupons in 4.20-7.875% range, ladder 2026-2055)
  - Junior subordinated debentures (5.5-6.5% range, multiple tranches)
  - Term loan (smaller scale, secured)
  - Revolving credit facility ($3B+ capacity, undrawn pre-WBD)
  - All bond debt was assumed by the post-Skydance-merger structure — PARA bond ticker continues to refer to these legacy obligations
- 2025 figures (post-merger combined entity, Aug 7 - Dec 31): Q4 2025 revenue $8.15B, adj OIBDA $612M, net loss to parent -$573M
- FY 2025 (full Paramount Global pre-merger Jan 1 - Aug 6 + post-merger Aug 7 - Dec 31): revenue $28.89B (-1.1%), adj EBITDA $3.8B (excluding $300M SBC), reported EBITDA $15.8B (the +75% YoY GAAP figure includes one-time merger-related accounting adjustments)
- 2026 guidance: revenue $30B (+4%), adj EBITDA $3.8B (flat) — guide implies modest revenue growth with margin pressure
- Net leverage standalone PSKY: ~$11-12B net debt / $3.8B EBITDA = ~3.0-3.2x
- Pending WBD acquisition financing: $77B cash equity component + $33B WBD debt assumption = $110B EV
  - $24B from Gulf sovereign wealth pledged (Saudi PIF / Mubadala / QIA referenced in FCC filing)
  - Remainder from PSKY cash on hand + new debt issuance + asset divestitures + potential additional equity
  - Combined-entity post-close debt likely $80-100B, EBITDA ~$15B+, leverage 5-7x at close
- Refi profile: standalone PSKY notes laddered through 2055; near-term maturities manageable. WBD bonds have change-of-control puts at 101% that bondholders may exercise post-close, forcing combined-entity refi

III. THESIS

The thesis is a serial M&A media holdco mid-second-transformation, with the WBD deal as the central credit-relevant event and Gulf sovereign financing as the structural wildcard. G.W.'s framework reads PARA bondholders as exposed to a sequence of merger integrations: (1) August 2025 Skydance merger closed and is in early integration, (2) WBD acquisition pending Q3 2026 close. The standalone PSKY (post-Skydance) is a stable-but-unspectacular credit: $30B 2026 revenue guide with only +4% growth, $3.8B adj EBITDA flat YoY, ~3.0x leverage. CBS broadcast + Pluto TV ad revenue + Paramount+ streaming subs + studio releases all show modest organic momentum. The Skydance merger consideration ($4.45B cash + Skydance equity contribution) was relatively modest, so post-Skydance leverage didn't blow out. The WBD acquisition changes everything. $77B cash + $33B WBD debt assumption = combined-entity debt potentially $80-100B at close. The $24B Gulf sovereign funding commitment is the structural innovation — Saudi PIF, Mubadala, QIA-style investors providing equity capital to absorb part of the cash consideration to WBD shareholders. The FCC foreign ownership filing is the critical regulatory milestone: foreign ownership of US broadcast licenses (CBS local stations, plus newly-acquired WBD stations if WBD owns any) requires FCC waiver. Without that approval, the Gulf financing structure unwinds and PSKY would need replacement financing at potentially higher cost. Combined-entity 5-7x leverage at close is the working assumption; deleveraging through synergies + asset sales over 2027-2029. G.W.'s heuristic — "distrust media issuers whose content cash burn is masked by accruals" + "distrust M&A integration timelines" — applies in spades. The PARA bondholders sit at the Paramount Global subsidiary level with structural senior position to the new parent equity; the change-of-control put on most tranches gives floor protection. Equity composite +16% 1m reflects market pricing the WBD deal close + Gulf financing acceptance.

IV. KEY RISKS

- WBD regulatory close risk. DOJ + EU + UK + Canada antitrust + FCC foreign ownership review. Any one block kills the deal. Combined entity would be #1 or #2 in US streaming, cable network programming, broadcast — antitrust scrutiny is comprehensive.
- Gulf sovereign financing falls through. $24B pledge depends on FCC foreign ownership approval. If denied, PSKY needs replacement financing at potentially higher cost (debt or equity), which compresses combined-entity credit metrics.
- Combined-entity leverage at close. 5-7x leverage on $15B EBITDA with $3-4B annual interest expense at higher coupons. Each year of synergy delay = ~$200-500M of additional interest cost burden.
- Skydance merger integration. Aug 2025 merger is only ~9 months in. If standalone PSKY underperforms 2026 guide, the WBD merger integration starts on a weaker base.
- Streaming sub trajectory. Paramount+ has been growing but burning cash. Combined Max + Paramount+ post-WBD-close has scale but also dual-platform integration complexity.
- CBS broadcast advertising secular pressure. Linear TV ad budgets compressing; CBS dependency on NFL + sports rights for retention.
- Studio cycle. Paramount Pictures + Skydance + WB combined = ~50% of US theatrical box office potential. Hit-driven business; bad year of releases compresses cash flow at exactly the wrong time.
- Change-of-control puts. PARA bondholders may put at 101% post-close. If majority puts, combined entity must refi billions at potentially distressed-of-class spreads.
- Paramount Global subsidiary structural position. Bonds at the operating subsidiary; if combined entity fails, operating subsidiary creditors have priority over parent equity but are exposed to operating-subsidiary cash flow specifically.

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Skydance merger closed August 7, 2025: Paramount Class A shareholders received $4.45B cash + Skydance equity contribution; new parent Paramount Skydance Corp (CIK 2041610, ticker PSKY) formed; legacy PARA + PARAA tickers delisted. Q4 2025 (post-merger first full quarter): revenue $8.15B, adj OIBDA $612M, net loss to parent -$573M. FY 2025: revenue $28.89B (-1.1%), adj EBITDA $3.8B (ex $300M SBC). 2026 guide: revenue $30B (+4%), adj EBITDA $3.8B (flat). WBD acquisition: announced Feb 27, 2026, $31/share cash, $110.9B EV; WBD shareholders approved 2026-04-23; expected close Q3 2026 pending DOJ + EU + UK + Canada + FCC foreign ownership review. $24B Gulf sovereign financing pledged to fund cash component. Equity tape: $11.09 close, 52w range $8.62-$20.86 (20.2% of range — well off the high), 5d +1.09%, 20d +16.49%, 20d vol 57.4% — equity has been crushed during 2025 on streaming losses + WBD deal complexity. Today equity +8.3% on the day per equity_monitor — likely on incremental WBD deal-progress news. PARA bonds at Paramount Global subsidiary level — XBRL data limited because the new parent CIK only has post-merger filings. No 8-Ks in bundle's 90-day window beyond the recent merger context.

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- WBD deal regulatory approvals — DOJ, EU, UK, Canada antitrust + FCC foreign ownership. Any 8-K disclosing extended timeline or conditions
- FCC foreign ownership ruling on Gulf sovereign financing — most idiosyncratic risk; denial would force replacement financing
- WBD deal close — Q3 2026 target; slip into Q4 2026 = financing terms reset
- Combined-entity financing details disclosure — bond/loan/equity issuance, total debt structure at close
- Change-of-control put activity on PARA bonds — bondholder elections at WBD close
- Standalone PSKY Q1 2026 print (expected May 2026) — first read on standalone trajectory in WBD integration year
- Paramount+ subscriber metrics — quarterly disclosure; >70M = on-track; <65M = streaming weakness
- CBS Sports content commentary — NFL renewal cycle, NBA/NHL discussions
- Box office cycle — Paramount + Skydance studio output Q2-Q4 2026
- PARA bond secondary spreads — tightening = deal certainty rising; widening = financing/regulatory concern
- Combined-entity synergy guide — Paramount-Skydance has indicated $3B+ over 24 months; quarterly disclosures matter
- Q4 2026 / FY 2026 print — first full year as merged Skydance entity, with WBD pending or just closed

coverage_memos.memo_md:
SATS — EchoStar Corp.
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: initiation
Quarters covered: 2024-Q1 to 2025-Q3 (Q4 2025 / FY 2025 print Feb 2026; AT&T spectrum sale closing mid-2026; DBS bond restructuring March 2026)
Date: 2026-05-01

I. SNAPSHOT

EchoStar is the post-2024 merged satellite + wireless + spectrum holdco — combines legacy DISH Network satellite TV (declining, ~7M subs), Boost Mobile (wireless retail, build-out failed), Hughes Communications (satellite broadband for residential + enterprise), and Charlie Ergen's accumulated spectrum portfolio (the central asset). The credit lens here is the G.W. spectrum-economics playbook: subscriber economics (DISH decline + Boost) × spectrum amortization (the central credit asset is the spectrum, valued via market transactions) × leverage capacity (transformed by 2025-2026 monetization). ML L4: Telecommunications / Telecom - Satellite. The story is the spectrum monetization wave: AT&T announced August 2025 to acquire $22.65B of 600MHz + 3.45GHz licenses (closing mid-2026 pending FCC); SpaceX signed September 2025 for $8.5B AWS-4 + H-Block + S-band, plus committed $2B of interest payment funding through November 2027. Total spectrum monetization $42B+ vs $26.7B existing debt — the franchise is transforming from distressed satellite operator to net-cash-rich strategic-asset holder. DISH DBS Restructuring Support Agreement reached March 19, 2026 with 82%+ creditor support: $75M cash settlement, eliminates DBS SubscriberCo financing layer, dismisses pending litigation. Equity composite neutral to bullish: $123.14 close (52w range $14.90-$137.44), 6m +64.6% — the equity already prices the transformation but transaction-execution risk remains.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE

- Total debt $26.71B at Q3 2025 (per XBRL DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount); $26.31B incl capital leases
- LT debt noncurrent $21.79B + current $4.52B = $26.31B funded at the corporate level
- Debt fair value $29.80B at Q3 (trading above par on spectrum sale narrative — meaningful market signal)
- Cash $2.43B Q3 2025; net debt ~$24.3B pre-spectrum-sale
- Tranche stack (per typical EchoStar/DISH structure):
  - DISH DBS Corp senior notes (multiple tranches, the legacy DBS subsidiary debt — central to the March 2026 RSA)
  - DISH Network Corp convertible notes
  - EchoStar senior unsecured / secured notes (multi-tranche, post-merger structure)
  - Boost Mobile / spectrum-collateralized term loans (some specifically secured by spectrum licenses)
  - Substantial maturity wall in 2026-2030
- Q3 2025 GAAP optic was disastrous: Op Income -$16.94B, NI -$12.78B — the Q3 hit was a non-cash impairment of DBS subscriber relationships and goodwill triggered by the spectrum sale agreements (which crystallized that DBS was no longer the key value driver)
- Q3 2025 interest expense $39.2M (Q3 alone — quarterly cash interest is ~$160M, suggesting some capitalized interest treatment)
- Maturities of senior debt YTD Q3: $622.7M; proceeds from new senior debt $150M; repayments capital lease $60M
- Post-spectrum-sale picture: $42B+ cash inflow vs $26.7B debt = potential net cash position $15B+ assuming all transactions close
- Refi profile: post-deal close, the entire credit profile restructures. Pre-deal, 2026-2028 refi tower was potentially distressed-exchange territory; post-deal, refi or full repayment becomes optional for management

III. THESIS

The thesis is a spectrum-asset-monetization story that transforms a distressed satellite operator into a net-cash-rich strategic holdco. G.W.'s spectrum-amortization lens reads SATS as the textbook example of the discipline: Charlie Ergen accumulated 600MHz, 700MHz, 3.45GHz, AWS-3, AWS-4, H-Block spectrum across 15+ years of FCC auctions, paid down to today's debt-financed positions, and is now monetizing $42B+ of spectrum at multiples that rebuild equity and bond value. The AT&T deal at $22.65B for 600MHz + 3.45GHz pencils to ~$1.30/MHzPop (roughly market clearing for low/mid-band today). The SpaceX deal at $8.5B for AWS-4 + H-Block + S-band rights is more strategic (SpaceX needs S-band rights for direct-to-device satellite service). The combined $42B+ of cash from completed/agreed monetization vs $26.7B of existing debt is the structural inflection — post-close (mid-2026), SATS would have meaningful net cash and substantially reduced refi risk on remaining tranches. The DISH DBS RSA in March 2026 cleaned up the legacy DBS bond complex: $75M cash settlement to bondholders, elimination of the DBS SubscriberCo subordination structure, dismissal of all pending litigation. This was a credit-positive resolution that avoided a forced restructuring/bankruptcy at the DBS subsidiary level. The subscriber economics are deteriorating but no longer central: DISH satellite TV continues losing subs (cord-cutting endgame), Boost Mobile didn't achieve standalone wireless build-out, Hughes broadband is steady. Post-deals, SATS becomes a "pure-play spectrum and satellite operator" with reduced leverage and optional growth (D2D satellite via SpaceX, possible more spectrum sales). G.W.'s heuristic — "distrust telecom names whose ARPU growth is from price hikes amid declining sub bases" — applied historically to DISH; post-restructure, the franchise is no longer ARPU-dependent. The credit is now "how much net cash + remaining spectrum value vs remaining debt obligations", and the math favors bondholders. Bonds trading above par at $29.8B fair value vs $26.7B carrying confirms the market read.

IV. KEY RISKS

- AT&T deal close risk. $22.65B closing mid-2026 pending FCC approval. FCC has historically taken 6-18 months on spectrum transfers; any second request or political delay extends timeline. SATS planned for closing-by-mid-2026 — slip to 2027 means continued cash burn and further refi pressure.
- SpaceX $8.5B close timing. Less certain than AT&T (no fixed close date publicly stated); separate FCC processes for different spectrum bands.
- DBS subscriber acceleration. ~7M subs declining at ~10-15% per year. If acceleration to 20%+ or major customer-churn event, DBS unit value craters faster than monetization can offset.
- Boost Mobile wind-down vs sale. Boost has been operationally unsuccessful as a standalone MNO. Either continued cash burn or sale to a major (T-Mobile? Verizon?) at a discount; either way, drag on EchoStar overall.
- Hughes broadband secular decline vs Starlink. Starlink is taking share in residential satellite broadband; Hughes is structurally challenged. Segment EBITDA likely declining 10%+ per year.
- DBS RSA execution. 82%+ creditor support is strong but not unanimous. Holdouts could litigate further or impose execution friction.
- Spectrum value mark to market. Remaining spectrum holdings (post AT&T + SpaceX) could be worth less if market clears below $1/MHzPop.
- Tax leakage on spectrum sales. Selling appreciated assets generates substantial capital gains tax; net-of-tax proceeds matter for credit math.
- Use of proceeds discipline. $42B+ cash inflow could be deployed to debt paydown (credit-positive), buybacks (credit-neutral), special dividends (credit-negative), or M&A (uncertain). Charlie Ergen has historically been opportunistic on capital allocation.

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Q3 2025: revenue $11.21B cumulative (Q3 quarterly ~$3.6B), Op Income -$16.94B (massive Q3 GAAP impairment, likely DBS subscriber/goodwill writedown reflecting spectrum sale crystallizing the value story away from DBS), NI -$12.78B. EBITDA proxy meaningless given the impairment. LT debt $21.79B noncurrent + $4.52B current = $26.31B; cash $2.43B; net debt ~$24.3B. Spectrum monetization timeline: Aug 2025 — AT&T deal $22.65B announced, closing mid-2026; Sept 2025 — SpaceX deal $8.5B + $2B interest payment funding through Nov 2027 announced. March 19, 2026 — DISH DBS Restructuring Support Agreement with 82%+ creditor support; $75M cash settlement; eliminates DBS SubscriberCo financing layer; dismisses pending litigation. Total spectrum monetization $42B+ vs $26.7B existing debt = potential net cash position $15B+ post-close. Equity composite neutral: $123.14 close, 52w range $14.90-$137.44 (88.3% of range), 5d +1.33%, 20d +2.11%, 1m +5.2%, 3m +8.5%, 6m +64.6%, 20d vol 55.7%, 90d realized vol 52.7% (66th pct, normal). The 6m +64% rally is the spectrum-monetization repricing. Bond fair value $29.8B vs $26.7B carrying is the credit market's vote of confidence on spectrum execution.

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- AT&T spectrum deal FCC approval — any 8-K disclosing FCC action or extended timeline. Slip past Q3 2026 = thesis recalibration
- SpaceX deal close progress — separate FCC processes for AWS-4, H-Block, S-band; quarterly disclosure milestones
- DBS subscriber count — quarterly disclosure; -20%+ YoY decline = collapse in DBS unit value
- Use of $42B+ proceeds — debt paydown announcement, buyback authorization, dividend, M&A. Capital allocation 8-Ks
- DBS RSA execution milestones — final restructuring documents, holdout litigation, financing layer changes
- Boost Mobile strategic alternatives — sale announcement to major MNO would be material credit event
- Hughes Communications quarterly performance — Starlink competition impact on subscriber and revenue
- Spectrum secondary market pricing — $/MHzPop in subsequent FCC auctions or private transactions; if 600MHz clears below $0.80/MHzPop, remaining spectrum value compresses
- Bond secondary spreads — currently bonds trade above par; tightening = continued credit improvement, widening = transaction execution doubt
- Q4 2025 / Q1 2026 prints — first read on operating performance post-restructuring
- Tax disclosure on spectrum sales — net-of-tax proceeds vs gross headlines

Sign: — G.W.

SBGI — Sinclair Television Group Inc.
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: refresh (v2 — Q1 2026 10-Q + 4/30 earnings call)
Quarters covered: 2024-Q2 to 2026-Q1
Date: 2026-05-11

I. SNAPSHOT
The post-Diamond Sports cleanup story — substantially complete. Sinclair operates a large broadcast portfolio with top-30 Big-4 affiliations across DC, Seattle, Portland OR, St. Louis, Nashville, Salt Lake City, Baltimore, Pittsburgh (heavy NBC + FOX bias) plus the Tennis Channel and the Ventures portfolio. Q1 2026 print delivered the cleanest standalone broadcast result since the pre-Diamond era. Media / Media Content. Net leverage 5.1x (improved 0.2x sequential), first-lien 3.8x, net first-lien 1.5x — substantially cleaner cap-structure-tier protection than the cohort headline implies.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE (Q1 2026 / 3/31/26 from 10-Q + earnings call)
- **Total debt: $4.4B** (from transcript; xbrl_financials LT debt field still patchy post-Diamond restructure).
- **Cash: $844M** ($392M at STG, $451M at Ventures) — fifth-highest absolute cash in the primer cohort relative to debt.
- Total liquidity: ~$1.5B.
- **Net leverage: 5.1x** (-0.2x sequential improvement); first-lien 3.8x; **net first-lien 1.5x** (excellent secured cover).
- April 2026 action: $165M term loan retirement via reverse Dutch auction → $12M annual cash interest savings.
- Maturity wall: 2026-2027 manageable; mid-decade refi cliff 2028-2031.
- Interest coverage: ~1.7x on Q1 EBITDA proxy $92M vs $76M Q1 interest (cohort-typical odd-year compression).

III. THESIS
Sinclair's Q1 2026 print is the cohort's cleanest fundamental read. Net income POSITIVE $20M — a turnaround from -$156M in Q1 2025, the cleanest standalone earnings result in 6+ quarters. Adj EBITDA $126M (+13% YoY), distribution rev $458M (+2% YoY), core ad $305M (+4% YoY). The Diamond Sports overhang is functionally gone; the JSA/LMA buy-ins are "substantially complete" with full $30M annualized synergies expected in 2026. Tennis Channel had its most-watched month ever in March (Indian Wells + Miami Open). Digital Remedy acquisition closed March, contributing to the +4% core ad growth via cross-channel ad platform capability. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance citing "resilient revenue mix, strong midterm political revenue expectations, a sports-heavy broadcast calendar headlined by the World Cup, and continued cost discipline" despite "consumer sentiment has moved meaningfully lower, inflation expectations have ticked higher." The negative is the structural JSA/LMA exposure — buy-ins reduce attribution risk but historical FCC posture-shifts are a tail. The April $165M term-loan retirement at a discount via reverse Dutch auction is a positive credit signal — Sinclair has the cash and discipline to opportunistically reduce gross debt rather than build to cash.

IV. KEY RISKS
- FCC attribution-rule tightening — Sinclair's residual JSA/LMA exposure (post substantially-complete buy-ins, a small number remain) is the cohort-tail.
- Reverse retrans pressure on NBC/FOX — Sinclair's NBC + FOX bias concentrates the reverse-retrans renewal counterparty risk on the sports-rights-cost-heavy networks. Next NFL rights cycle (late this decade) is the structural ceiling on net retrans.
- Diamond Sports tail — any residual contingent liability from the Diamond bankruptcy (intercompany guarantees, transition agreements, environmental/regulatory) that surfaces in 2026 is a credit setback.
- Macro consumer ad — management explicitly flagged "consumer sentiment moved meaningfully lower" — Q1 +4% core ad was Olympic-aided; Q2-Q3 core ad faces a tougher comp.
- Cash buildup vs deployment — $844M cash + $1.5B total liquidity is the cohort-high absolute cushion. Capital allocation discipline (more reverse Dutch auctions vs equity buyback) is the watch item.

SIRI — Sirius XM Radio LLC (parent: Sirius XM Holdings Inc.)
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: initiation
Quarters covered: 2024-Q1 to 2025-Q4 (Q4/FY 2025 print 2026-02-05; Q1 2026 print expected late April / early May 2026)
Date: 2026-05-01

I. SNAPSHOT

Sirius XM is the US satellite radio monopoly (33M paid subs) plus Pandora streaming (5.6M self-pay subs) — a subscription audio platform with monopoly satellite-radio infrastructure and a struggling streaming-radio side property. The credit lens here is the G.W. subscription-audio playbook: subscriber economics (self-pay subs x ARPU − SAC ÷ churn), content/talent amortization (Howard Stern + sports + creator deals), and capital-return discipline given high FCF conversion. ML L4: Media / Media Content. The credit-relevant facts: FY 2025 revenue $8.56B (-2% YoY); FY 2025 adj EBITDA ~$2.5B; net leverage **3.6x** at YE 2025 (target low-to-mid-3x by late 2026); debt reduction $669M in 2025 (including $371M in Q4); 2026 guide revenue ~$8.5B (flat), adj EBITDA ~$2.6B, FCF $1.35B (target $1.5B by 2027); additional $100M cost savings exiting 2026 = $350M cumulative cost program. Net income FY 2025 $805M (vs -$2.07B prior year — the prior year was distorted by Liberty Sirius Group merger / impairment noise). Equity (SIRI) at $26.94 close, **79.8% of 52w range**, 1m +17%, 3m +34%, 6m +26%, composite **bullish** but trend_divergence flagged today (5d -3.8% vs tmt median +0.4%) — modest pullback after a strong 6m run. This is the **highest-quality credit in the G.W. coverage list** by net leverage and FCF profile.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE

- LT debt not in XBRL bundle directly (mgmt-disclosed); estimated **~$10.0B gross** at YE 2025 based on 3.6x net leverage x $2.5B adj EBITDA + ~$80M cash = ~$9B net.
- Cash $79M Q3 2025 (very thin liquidity buffer for an entity this size — but FCF generation $1.35B/year covers maturities organically).
- Total debt reduction $669M in 2025 (incl. $371M in Q4 alone) — capital allocation toward deleveraging, not buybacks/dividends.
- LTM adj EBITDA ~$2.5B FY 2025 (mgmt-disclosed); 2026 guide ~$2.6B largely flat.
- Net leverage **3.6x** — target low-to-mid-3x by late 2026 (i.e., another $300-500M of net debt reduction in 2026).
- Interest expense Q3 2025 standalone $206M = ~$824M annualized (high coupon weight); coverage = $2.5B / $824M = **3.0x — strong** for a B/B+ media credit.
- Tranche stack: senior secured term loan + multi-tranche senior secured notes at the SiriusXM Radio LLC level (the operating sub that bondholders sit at); senior unsecured notes; revolver.
- Refi profile: laddered through 2027-2032; mgmt has been opportunistically refinancing inside the curve (the 2025 paydowns reduce 2027-2028 maturities specifically).
- Liquidity: $79M cash + revolver capacity (~$1.5B) = adequate; $1.35B FCF guide for 2026 covers maturities organically.
- Capex Q3 2025 standalone $190M; FY 2025 ~$680M; 2026 capex similar (satellite refresh cycle is mid-cycle).
- Capital allocation: deleveraging + dividend (LT dividend yield ~3-4%) + opportunistic buybacks; the prior LBO-style high-payout era under Liberty has shifted toward a balanced model post the 2024 spinoff.
- 9M 2025 CFO $1.22B = on track for FCF guide.

III. THESIS

The thesis is a stable subscription-audio credit with secular sub-decline pressure offset by ARPU defense and aggressive cost-cutting — and it's the **cleanest credit in the entire TMT cohort I'm reviewing this week**. G.W.'s framework reads SIRI through the subscription-economics lens first: 33M satellite radio paid subs is a slowly-eroding base (cars rolling off the program, EV adoption reducing the auto-subscription pipeline, OEM in-vehicle integration competing — Spotify, Apple Music, podcasts via CarPlay). Self-pay sub trends have been negative for years; mgmt offsets via ARPU increases (price hikes on plans), trial-conversion improvements, and Pandora streaming subscriber additions (5.6M self-pay is below where it should be vs Spotify/Apple competitive pressure). The credit-positive offsets: (1) the satellite radio infrastructure is a near-monopoly with high switching costs (you don't replace satellite radio infrastructure overnight); (2) FCF generation is exceptional — $1.35B 2026 guide → $1.5B 2027 target = 16-17% FCF margin on revenue, which is best-in-class for media; (3) 3.6x leverage with 3.0x interest coverage is investment-grade-style metrics on a B/B+ rated credit, leaving meaningful spread for re-rating; (4) debt reduction of $669M in 2025 = real deleveraging trajectory toward low-3x by late 2026. The cost program — $350M cumulative, $100M incremental in 2026 — is in execution mode. G.W.'s heuristic — "distrust telecom names whose ARPU growth is from price hikes amid declining sub bases" — applies here: SIRI is essentially in this mode (ARPU hikes offsetting sub declines), so the EBITDA stability is real but volume-driven growth is gone. The differentiator vs IHRT (which is also seeing terrestrial declines + digital growth): SIRI has higher absolute leverage but stronger coverage and FCF, plus a structural moat (satellite license + integrated auto distribution) that IHRT lacks. **Net read**: this is a B+/BB-quality credit at B-spread levels; carry play with embedded re-rating optionality if leverage hits low-3x by late 2026.

IV. KEY RISKS

- **Self-pay sub erosion acceleration.** 33M baseline; sustained -1.5M/year would push 2027 EBITDA $200M lower than guide; sustained -2M+/year would compress leverage above 4x.
- **EV / OEM integration disruption.** Tesla doesn't ship satellite-radio hardware; legacy OEMs are increasing in-vehicle streaming (Spotify, Apple) integration that competes with the SiriusXM trial-conversion funnel. Long-tail risk; quarterly trial conversion rates are the leading indicator.
- **Pandora secular weakness.** Pandora self-pay 5.6M is below where it was 5 years ago; if Pandora hits a sub-$0.5B revenue threshold, mgmt may divest or shut down ad-supported tier — an asset-light strategy.
- **Content cost inflation.** Howard Stern, NFL audio rights, MLB rights, Conan O'Brien podcast deal — these are 5-7 year amortization commitments; if next renewal cycle (2027-2028) prices materially higher, content-cost-to-revenue ratio expands.
- **ARPU price-hike exhaustion.** Price hikes have offset sub declines; if churn responds to next round of hikes (>$2/month), the offset breaks.
- **Capital allocation shift.** If mgmt redirects 2026 deleveraging cash to buybacks / dividends instead, the leverage trajectory stalls = ratings risk (Moody's / S&P have outlook positive on the deleveraging path).
- **Liberty Media / John Malone strategic action.** SIRI was spun out of Liberty Media in Sept 2024; legacy Liberty/Malone-affiliated holdings could trigger restructuring or M&A that reshapes the cap stack.
- **Antitrust / regulatory on auto-OEM bundles.** SiriusXM has trial bundling deals with most OEMs; any FTC action against OEM-bundled trials would damage the conversion funnel.

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Q3 2025 (printed 2025-10-XX): revenue $2.16B Q3 standalone (flat YoY), op income $498M Q3 standalone, 9M cumulative net income $706M (vs -$1.95B Q3 2024 YTD — prior year had massive Liberty merger noise), 9M CFO $1.22B. Net leverage 3.6x at YE 2025. SiriusXM 33M paid subs; Pandora 5.6M self-pay subs at YE 2025. 2026 guide: revenue ~$8.5B (flat), adj EBITDA ~$2.6B, FCF $1.35B (vs $1.5B target by 2027); additional $100M cost savings exiting 2026 (cumulative $350M cost program). Equity (SIRI) trading at $26.94 close, **79.8% of 52w range** ($19.71-$28.77), 5d -3.8%, 20d +15.1%, 1m +16.7%, 3m +34.3%, 6m +25.9%, 90d realized vol 37.4% (34th pct, **normal**). One flag today: trend_divergence (5d -3.8% vs tmt peers +0.4%, mag -0.04). Modest pullback after a multi-month rally. No daily_triage appearances in 30d. Q1 2026 print expected late April / early May 2026 (need to verify exact date).

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- **Q1 2026 print (late April / early May 2026):** revenue, adj EBITDA, self-pay sub trajectory, FCF, FY 2026 guide reaffirmation.

III. THESIS

The thesis is a satellite-operator deleveraging inflection that the equity tape is repricing aggressively (+67% 6m, +44% 1m, 99.9% of 52w range) and the bond side should re-rate toward — with the caveat that 1.4x interest coverage is still thin and the ViaSat-3 service ramp must hit on time. G.W.'s satellite-operator framework reads VSAT as moving from the capex-peak phase (FY24-FY26) into the revenue-ramp phase (FY26-FY28) as Flight 2 of ViaSat-3 comes online May 2026 and Flight 3 follows. Defense and Advanced Technologies is the credit-positive growth segment (mid-teens growth guide for FY26) — and the rumored defense spinoff is the equity-side catalyst that could unlock value for unsecured creditors via parent-level cash distribution. The Inmarsat integration is moving from cost-synergy realization (closed, captured) into cross-sell synergies (in-flight connectivity bundled with Inmarsat L-band safety services for airlines is the highest-value cross-sell). Net leverage at 3.25x is sector-leading for satellite-with-buildout; the 3.7x → 3.25x trajectory in 12 months proves the deleveraging is real, not just a multiple expansion. The credit-positive offsets to the thin coverage: $1.35B cash is large vs maturity profile; positive FCF guide in FY26 + FY27 ex-Ligado means organic deleveraging continues; Ligado windfall was used for term loan paydown rather than dividends/buybacks (capital allocation discipline). G.W.'s heuristic — "distrust telecom names whose ARPU growth is from price hikes amid declining sub bases" — does NOT apply here; ViaSat's growth is volume-driven (Defense, IFC seat ramp on Flight 2/3, Inmarsat global mobility) not price-extraction. The risk to the thesis is satellite operational: any ViaSat-3 satellite anomaly, launch failure, or in-orbit fault would re-set the FCF trajectory. Net read: this is the cleanest credit story in the distressed-tmt cohort I'm reviewing today; mid-B credit re-rating toward BB if Flight 2 hits service in Q1 FY27 on schedule.

IV. KEY RISKS

- **ViaSat-3 satellite operational risk.** Flight 1 had a known antenna deployment fault in 2023; Flight 2 launching service May 2026 must hit on time — any delay or in-orbit anomaly resets the FCF ramp by 12-18 months.
- **Interest coverage thin (1.4x).** Even with leverage improving to 3.25x, the absolute interest burden ($1.12B annualized) keeps coverage tight; one missed quarter compresses it below 1.3x.
- **Defense spinoff structure risk.** The rumored defense spinoff is equity-positive but credit treatment depends on structure — a tax-free spin with no debt allocation could leave the remaining commercial-satellite credit weaker; a sale-and-distribute structure would be credit-positive via parent cash deployment.
- **Inmarsat integration synergies.** Cost synergies largely captured; revenue synergies (in-flight connectivity cross-sell) are still in execution and could underdeliver.
- **Defense budget cycle.** Mid-teens revenue growth guide for FY26 D&AT segment is dependent on continued DoD satellite-capability spending; any 2026 budget reset would compress that growth rate.
- **In-flight connectivity competitive intensity.** Starlink is now winning IFC contracts (United, Air France-KLM); ViaSat must defend its existing IFC base while expanding into Inmarsat's airline customer base.
- **Capex re-acceleration.** FY26 guide $1.0-1.1B is the inflection; any new satellite program announced for FY27-FY28 would defer the FCF positive trajectory.
- **High volatility on the equity side (78% 90d realized vol, 93rd pct).** Vol-spike + relative-outperform + new-52w-high all flagged today = potential mean-reversion risk on the equity side, which would shift narrative tone vs the bonds.

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Q3 FY26 (printed 2026-02-05): revenue $1.2B (+3% YoY), EPS $0.79 vs -$0.46 expected — massive beat driven by Ligado settlement. 9M FY26 cumulative: revenue $3.47B, op income $108.7M, GAAP net loss -$92.9M (narrowing materially from -$170M Q2 YTD), CFO $1.27B (strong cash generation). Net debt $5.06B with leverage improved to 3.25x (vs 3.7x YoY); $300M term loan principal retired with Ligado proceeds; Inmarsat-to-Viasat cash movement program $350M moved of $400-500M target. ViaSat-3 Flight 2 launched November 2025, services commencing May 2026; Flight 3 launching shortly after. FY26 guide reaffirmed: low-single-digit revenue growth, flat adj EBITDA, mid-teens D&AT growth, capex $1.0-1.1B, positive FCF in FY26 + FY27 ex-Ligado. Equity (VSAT) at $65.91 close, **99.9% of 52w range** (52w range $8.61-$65.98 — that's a 7.7x absolute range — extraordinary recovery), 5d +5.3%, 20d +45.7%, 1m +44%, 3m +43%, 6m +67%, 90d realized vol 78.1% (93rd pct, **elevated**). Three flags raised today: vol_spike (mag 0.77), relative_outperform (mag +1.97 z-score, 1d +11.2% vs tmt peers), new_52w_high (100% of range). Q4 FY26 print expected late May 2026 (FY ends 2026-03-31).

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- **Q4/FY26 print (late May 2026):** revenue, adj EBITDA, FY27 guide, ViaSat-3 Flight 2 service-commencement confirmation.
- **ViaSat-3 Flight 2 service start (May 2026):** confirmation of service activation = FCF ramp begins; any delay = 6-12 months of pushed-out revenue.
- **ViaSat-3 Flight 3 launch:** "shortly after" Flight 2 — confirm timeline in the next print.
- **Net leverage trajectory:** 3.25x baseline; <3.0x by end-FY27 = clean deleveraging path; >3.5x = capex re-acceleration or EBITDA miss.
- **Interest coverage:** 1.4x baseline; <1.3x = liquidity concern even with $1.35B cash.
- **Defense spinoff announcement:** if mgmt formalizes the structure, credit treatment depends heavily on debt-allocation method — read 8-K closely.
- **D&AT revenue growth:** mid-teens guide for FY26; quarterly tracking shows DoD budget environment.
- **IFC contract wins/losses:** any United/Delta/Air France equivalent contract movement vs Starlink.
- **Inmarsat cash movement progress:** $350M of $400-500M moved; monitor for full target capture in FY26.
- **Equity vol mean-reversion:** 78% realized vol is unsustainable; a 20-30% pullback on profit-taking would not change the credit thesis but would re-frame the market narrative.

Sign: — G.W.

coverage_memos.memo_md:
VSNT — Versant Media Group Inc.
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: initiation
Quarters covered: FY 2025 standalone (printed 2026-03-03; first as-public-company; Q1 2026 prints 2026-05-14)
Date: 2026-05-01

I. SNAPSHOT

Versant Media Group is the brand-new Comcast spinoff that began trading Nasdaq on January 5, 2026 — Comcast separated its cable networks portfolio into a standalone public company effective 11:59 PM ET January 2, 2026. The franchise comprises USA Network, MS NOW (formerly MSNBC), CNBC, Syfy, E!, Oxygen, Golf Channel plus digital properties (GolfNow, Fandango Media, Rotten Tomatoes). Cable network-only structure — no broadcast, no streaming flagship, no studio. The credit lens here is the G.W. cable-network-programmer playbook: subscriber economics (linear sub fees + cable advertising — >80% pay TV revenue) × content amortization (sports rights at Golf Channel, NBC News content sublicensed to MS NOW, original programming at USA/Syfy) × leverage capacity (sub-1x — exceptionally clean). ML L4: Media / Cable & Satellite TV. FY 2025 (printed 2026-03-03 as standalone): revenue $6.69B (-5.3% YoY), net income $930M, adj EBITDA $2.42B / standalone adj EBITDA $2.18B. Q4 2025 standalone adj EBITDA $521M (-19% YoY — meaningful linear decline). Capital structure ~$983M debt / $55M cash + $1B buyback authorization. Mark Lazarus (former NBCU chairman) is CEO; Brian Roberts retains ~1/3 voting control via Class B shares. Equity composite bullish but tape neutral: $40.19 close (vs $45.17 IPO price, vs $59 52w high, 40.9% of range), 1m +8.6%, 3m +22.3%. Q1 2026 prints 2026-05-14 — first standalone-quarter print.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE

- Total debt ~$983M (per recent disclosures); debt-funded spinoff distribution from Comcast was modest relative to enterprise value
- Cash ~$55M; net debt ~$928M — extremely light for a $7B-revenue cable network programmer
- LTM standalone adj EBITDA $2.18B (FY 2025 mgmt-cited); reported adj EBITDA $2.42B (includes some allocations from parent)
- Net leverage ~0.4x standalone — by far the cleanest in the broadcaster/cable cohort
- Tranche stack: not yet disclosed in detail (first standalone 10-Q hasn't dropped). Spinoff documents suggest:
  - Senior secured term loan at the operating company (modest scale ~$500-700M)
  - Senior unsecured notes (~$300-500M, multiple tranches)
  - Revolving credit facility (multi-hundred-million capacity)
  - Maturity ladder TBD; spinoff debt typically issued with 5-7 year tenors → expect maturities 2031-2033
- Spinoff cash flow note: $1B buyback authorization signals management confidence; with ~$2B of standalone EBITDA and ~$1B debt, the franchise is significantly underleveraged for the asset class
- 2025 capex: not separately disclosed; cable network programmer capex typically <5% of revenue
- Non-pay-TV revenue 19% in 2025 ($826M from platforms revenue); CEO Lazarus targets 33% near-term, eventually closer to 50% — diversification away from declining linear is the strategic thesis
- The Comcast carve-out structure means content licensing arrangements with NBCUniversal exist — credit-relevant if those terms unwind unfavorably at renewal

III. THESIS

The thesis is a brand-new cable network programmer with a uniquely clean balance sheet, capable management, and a structural transformation imperative — but with a declining linear revenue base that will pressure the ratings agencies in 2026-2027. G.W.'s framework reads VSNT as the anti-leveraged-buyout of cable network spinoffs: most carve-outs (looking at WBD's pre-Skydance situation) come out levered 4-5x with thin equity cushion; VSNT comes out at sub-1x net leverage with $1B of buyback authorization. The strategic choice was deliberate — Comcast positioned Versant for capital flexibility rather than maximum tax-efficient debt extraction. The structural pressure is real: revenue -5.3% YoY in 2025 ($7.06B → $6.69B), Q4 standalone adj EBITDA -19% YoY ($521M from $643M implied PY) — these are cable industry secular trajectories. Revenue is 80%+ pay TV = subscribers + affiliate fees from MVPDs, both declining structurally. CEO Lazarus's strategic pivot to 33% non-pay-TV revenue (and eventually 50%) is the right answer: GolfNow (golf course tee-time bookings), Fandango (movie tickets), Rotten Tomatoes (ad-supported review platform), MSNBC streaming subscriptions, USA streaming. These are higher-growth digital assets that can offset linear decline if executed. The MS NOW rebrand (from MSNBC, completed alongside the spinoff) signals Comcast's walk-away from a high-controversy news brand and a clean reset for VSNT. G.W.'s heuristic — "distrust media issuers whose content cash burn is masked by accruals" — applies softly: VSNT inherits NBC Sports / NBC News content licensing relationships that are real cash flows, not accrual gaps. The credit math is straightforward: at sub-1x leverage, VSNT could absorb 40%+ of EBITDA decline before leverage breached 2.0x. The Q1 2026 print on May 14 is the binary event: standalone trajectory (revenue -5%, EBITDA -15-20%) vs management's transformation plan execution. Equity at $40 (down from $45 IPO; -32% from 52w high $59) reflects the market's skepticism on linear secular trajectory; bondholders sit much higher in the capital stack.

IV. KEY RISKS

- Linear cable network revenue decline accelerating. -5.3% FY 2025 is the trajectory; if Q1 2026 prints -7-8%, the structural pressure on multi-year EBITDA worsens.
- MVPD subscriber cancellation acceleration. Cable network programmers depend on bundled distribution; if cord-cutting accelerates beyond -8%/year, revenue + distribution renegotiation pressure compounds.
- Comcast-VSNT relationship terms. Versant inherits content licensing arrangements with NBCUniversal (NBC Sports, NBC News) at terms negotiated before the spinoff. Renewal in 5-7 years could shift economics unfavorably.
- Sports rights cost inflation at Golf Channel. PGA Tour, LPGA, European Tour rights renewals — Versant has Golf Channel as a meaningful asset, but content cost is escalating across sports.
- MS NOW rebranding execution. The MSNBC → MS NOW transition is risky for ratings continuity. Linear ad revenue decline could accelerate during transition.
- CEO transition / strategic execution. Lazarus is an experienced operator but he's executing a bottom-up transformation in a declining industry. Strategic plan execution is the next 3-year credit narrative.
- $1B buyback authorization vs deleveraging optionality. With sub-1x leverage already, the buyback signals capital return over deleveraging. Rationale is sound for an underleveraged credit, but if EBITDA declines faster than expected, buyback execution could push leverage up just when the credit is weakening.
- Brian Roberts Class B voting control. ~1/3 voting power via Class B shares means strategic decisions could be driven by parent-related considerations (NBC content strategy, NBCU relationship) rather than VSNT-standalone optimization.
- Brand-new public-company disclosure cadence. Q1 2026 will be first standalone quarter; full picture of capital structure, segment economics, and management priorities still emerging.

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Spinoff completed January 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET; Versant began trading Nasdaq January 5, 2026 at $45.17. FY 2025 results (printed 2026-03-03 first standalone): revenue $6.69B (-5.3% YoY from $7.06B), net income $930M, adj EBITDA $2.42B, standalone adj EBITDA $2.18B. Q4 2025 standalone adj EBITDA $521M (-19% YoY — meaningful linear decline). 80%+ revenue from pay TV. Non-pay-TV revenue 19% / $826M from platforms (GolfNow, Fandango, Rotten Tomatoes); CEO target 33% near-term, 50% longer-term. Capital structure: ~$983M debt / $55M cash. $1B buyback authorization. Mark Lazarus CEO; Brian Roberts retains ~1/3 voting via Class B. Q1 2026 results expected 2026-05-14 (first standalone-quarter print). Equity tape: $40.19 close (vs $45.17 IPO, vs $59 52w high), 52w range $27.17-$59.00 (40.9% of range), 5d -0.74%, 20d +8.10%, 1m +8.6%, 3m +22.3%, 20d vol 27.8%, 90d realized vol 37.1% (34th pct, normal). Equity has stabilized after initial post-IPO dropout; bullish 3m on transformation thesis. No 8-Ks in bundle's 90-day window beyond the spinoff completion.

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- Q1 2026 print 2026-05-14: first standalone quarter; revenue trajectory vs FY -5.3% baseline, standalone adj EBITDA vs Q4 $521M
- Non-pay-TV revenue mix progress: 19% → 33% target trajectory; quarterly disclosure
- MSNBC/MS NOW ratings post-rebrand — if material decline, signals brand-equity loss
- Golf Channel sports rights renewals (PGA Tour, LPGA) — content cost inflation
- Buyback execution rate against $1B authorization — pace + timing vs leverage trajectory
- Net leverage trajectory: sub-1x baseline; 2.0x = thesis broken (would require either major M&A or substantial buyback)
- Any M&A — VSNT is a likely consolidator or consolidation target in cable network sector
- NBCUniversal content licensing relationship updates (NBC Sports, NBC News content — pricing, exclusivity)
- Linear advertising revenue Q2-Q4 2026 — sector benchmark
- USA Network original programming slate — flagship content
- Streaming subscription bundling commentary — affiliated streaming offerings (Peacock relationship)
- Any 8-K announcing dividend initiation, special dividend, or refi

Sign: — G.W.

coverage_memos.memo_md:
WBD — Warner Bros. Discovery (Discovery Global Holdings)
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: initiation
Quarters covered: 2024-Q1 to 2025-Q3 (Q4 2025 / FY 2025 print Feb 2026; Q1 2026 print expected May 2026; pending Paramount Skydance acquisition close Q3 2026)
Date: 2026-05-01

I. SNAPSHOT

Warner Bros. Discovery is the merged Warner Media + Discovery entity (the 2022 AT&T spinoff/merger), one of the largest US media franchises by content library scope: HBO Max streaming, Warner Bros. studios (movies + TV), DC Comics, CNN, TBS/TNT/TruTV cable networks, Discovery+/Discovery channels, sports rights (NBA, NHL, MLB regional), international networks. The credit lens here is the G.W. media-content playbook: subscriber economics (Max + linear) × content amortization (HBO/sports rights cash spend vs accrual) × leverage capacity (3.0x current vs covenant runway). ML L4: Media / Media Content. The defining event is the pending Paramount Skydance acquisition: $110.9B enterprise value, $31/share cash to WBD shareholders (147% premium to unaffected $12.54), shareholder vote passed 2026-04-23 overwhelmingly, expected close Q3 2026 subject to DOJ/EU/UK/Canada regulatory clearances. The credit story is now binary: WBD as a standalone deleveraging media franchise vs WBD as a piece of a combined Paramount-Skydance-WBD mega-cap entity. Equity at $27.05 (86.6% of 52w range, +28.9% 6m) is pricing close-and-arb-spread.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE

- Total long-term debt $33.52B at Q3 2025 (per XBRL); current portion $139M
- Material deleveraging: $43.67B YE 2023 → $39.51B YE 2024 → $33.52B Q3 2025 = $10B+ paid down in 18 months via FCF + asset sales
- Cash $4.29B Q3 2025; net debt ~$29.2B
- LTM adj EBITDA implied $9-10B (Q3 2025 EBITDA proxy $4.76B was unusually high — quarterly typically $2.5-3.5B); industry-typical adj EBITDA for WBD ~$9-10B FY
- Net leverage ~3.0-3.5x WBD standalone
- Tranche stack (per typical WBD/Discovery legacy structure):
  - Discovery Communications legacy senior unsecured notes (multiple tranches, 3.95-7.0% coupons, ladder 2026-2055)
  - Time Warner / WarnerMedia legacy bonds (assumed in 2022 merger, multiple tranches)
  - Term Loan A (smaller scale, secured)
  - Revolving credit facility ($6B+ capacity, undrawn)
- Q3 2025 interest expense $515M = annualized ~$2.0B against $33.5B = 6.0% blended cost
- Refi profile: laddered through 2055; near-term maturities manageable; 2027-2028 has multi-billion refi tower
- The pending Paramount Skydance transaction: WBD debt is assumed by the combined entity; existing WBD bondholders likely get change-of-control put at 101% on most tranches (standard HY indenture clause). Combined entity post-deal will carry WBD debt + Paramount debt + new financing for the $77B cash equity payment to WBD shareholders
- Financing for the cash component: Paramount Skydance has indicated a mix of cash on hand + new debt + equity issuance. Specific financing structure not yet detailed publicly

III. THESIS

The thesis is a deleveraging media credit being acquired at a transformative premium, with all the standard merger-arb credit angles plus a content-cash-vs-accrual question that hangs over the combined entity. G.W.'s subscriber-economics lens reads WBD's standalone trajectory as positive: the franchise was deleveraging credibly ($10B+ paid down in 18 months), Max streaming sub growth was steady, sports rights renewals (NBA loss to Amazon was a 2024 negative; remaining MLB/NHL relationships intact), and the 2024 GAAP impairment cycle (-$22B+ of net losses across 2024 driven by goodwill writedowns) is fully behind. Content-amortization risk had been the central concern: HBO content cash spend running $20B+ annually vs lower amortization expense on the income statement = persistent accrual gap that GAAP financials masked. The Paramount transaction changes everything. At $31/share = $77B equity + $33B debt = $110B EV, this is roughly 11x trailing EBITDA on the standalone WBD franchise — a premium multiple that reflects strategic value rather than financial economics. For credit holders, the question is not WBD-standalone trajectory but what does the combined Paramount+Skydance+WBD entity look like: combined ~$50-60B revenue, ~$15B EBITDA, debt stack that includes WBD's $33B + Paramount's existing ~$15B + new financing for the cash component (likely $30-50B more) = combined funded debt potentially $80-100B at close. At closing, leverage on the combined entity could be 5-7x — that's the credit-relevant question. WBD's existing bonds are protected by change-of-control puts (101% standard) and the deal's investment-grade-ish target rating (likely BB/Ba1 or low-IG) — but post-close credit profile depends entirely on synergy realization, which in media M&A historically delivers 60-80% of announced figures. G.W.'s heuristic — "distrust media issuers whose content cash burn is masked by accruals" + "distrust M&A integration timelines" + "distrust 'synergies' called out in the second post-merger year" — applies in triplicate here. The deal closes Q3 2026 if regulatory clears; until then, WBD bonds trade as a merger-arb instrument with the change-of-control put as the floor.

IV. KEY RISKS

- Regulatory close risk. DOJ + EU + UK + Canada all reviewing. Any one blocking or imposing material divestitures could break the deal. Combined entity would be #1 or #2 in US streaming, cable network programming, and content production — antitrust scrutiny is real.
- Combined-entity leverage at close. Post-close 5-7x leverage on combined entity is plausible. If synergies underperform announced figures, deleveraging trajectory stretches into 2028-2029. Refi at higher coupons compounds.
- Sports rights amortization gap. WBD pays cash for NBA/MLB/NHL rights up front (or in tranches) but amortizes over the life of the contract. The combined entity inherits this accrual gap on top of Paramount's CBS sports rights.
- Streaming sub trajectory. Max + Paramount+ both face Netflix + Disney+ + Amazon scale advantages. Combined entity has scale but dual-platform integration risk for 18-24 months post-close.
- Linear cable network secular decline. WBD cable networks (TNT, TBS, CNN, Discovery, HGTV, Food Network) face cord-cutting; combined with Paramount's MTV, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon = doubled exposure to linear decline.
- Change-of-control put execution. Most WBD bonds have 101% put on change of control. Bondholders may put at par+1, forcing combined entity to refi at potentially higher rates depending on market conditions at close.
- CEO transition / leadership uncertainty. David Zaslav (current WBD CEO) role post-close uncertain. Paramount Skydance leadership integration adds organizational complexity.
- Studio cycle dependency. WB/DC and Paramount studio output is hit-driven. A bad year of theatrical releases compresses combined-entity cash flow.

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Q3 2025 (reflected in bundle): revenue $27.84B cumulative through 9 months, net income $979M (vs -$22B+ cumulative loss in 2024 — major GAAP turnaround), Q3 alone op income $389M, EBITDA proxy $4.76B Q3, FCF Q3 cumulative $2.52B - $810M capex = $1.7B FCF cumulative. Q3 LT debt $33.52B (down $4B from YE 2024). Q3 interest expense $515M cumulative through three quarters → annualized $686M wait that doesn't match — likely $515M is Q3 alone. Paramount Skydance merger timeline: Feb 27, 2026 — formal agreement signed; April 23, 2026 — WBD shareholder approval vote passed overwhelmingly; deal terms $31/share cash, $110.9B EV, 147% premium to unaffected $12.54. Expected close Q3 2026, pending DOJ + EU + UK + Canada antitrust review. Equity composite bearish (label) but tape neutral: $27.05 close, 52w range $8.06-$30.00 (86.6% of range), 1m -1.5%, 3m -2.0%, 6m +28.9%, 20d vol 8.89%, 90d realized vol 14.1% (1st pct, very low) — characteristic of merger-arb instrument trading near deal price. No 8-Ks in bundle's 90-day window. The merger-arb spread (deal price $31 vs current $27.05) is ~14%, reflecting modest deal-break probability discount + time-to-close.

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- DOJ / EU / UK / Canada regulatory action — any objections, second requests, or extended timelines from any jurisdiction
- Deal break headlines — WBD board recommendation reversal (already passed), Paramount funding issues, antitrust block. Equity gap-down to $20 = deal-break probability rising materially
- Combined-entity financing structure announcement — Paramount-Skydance must arrange funding for $77B cash component. Bond / loan / preferred / equity issuance disclosures matter
- Change-of-control put activity — bondholder elections post-close
- WBD Q1 2026 earnings (expected May 2026): standalone trajectory — revenue, EBITDA, FCF, sub trends — pre-close
- Combined synergy guidance — Paramount-Skydance has indicated ~$3B in cost synergies over 24 months; quarterly disclosures matter
- WBD bond secondary spreads — tighten = deal certainty rising; widen = deal-break repricing
- Paramount Skydance equity / debt issuance announcements — capital structure for the close
- Streaming sub disclosures (Max + Paramount+) — pre-close standalone, post-close combined
- Theatrical box office cycle — WB and Paramount studios both in slump risk
- Q3 2025 quarterly EBITDA proxy $4.76B looked unusually elevated — Q4 2025 print (already past) would have normalized; Q1 2026 print is the next data point

Sign: — G.W.

coverage_memos.memo_md:
WIN — Windstream Services LLC (bond issuer; parent: Uniti Group Inc. / UNIT, post 2025-08-01 merger)
Sector: tmt | Analyst: G.W. | Coverage: core
Memo type: initiation
Quarters covered: 2024-Q1 to 2025-Q4 (Q4/FY 2025 print 2026-03-02 under combined UNIT entity; WIN standalone breakouts ended at the August 2025 merger close)
Date: 2026-05-01

I. SNAPSHOT

Windstream Services is the bond-issuing operating subsidiary of legacy Windstream Holdings, which on 2025-08-01 became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Uniti Group Inc. (NASDAQ: UNIT). The combined entity is a US fiber/wireline insurgent — three reporting segments: Kinetic (legacy Windstream consumer/SMB broadband), Uniti Solutions (mid-market enterprise), and Fiber Infrastructure (the legacy Uniti REIT-style dark-fiber/lit-services lease book). The credit lens here is the G.W. wireline+towers-hybrid playbook: subscriber economics in Kinetic x lease-income visibility in Fiber Infrastructure x consolidated leverage capacity. ML L4: Telecommunications / Telecom - Wireline Integrated & Services. The credit-relevant facts: combined long-term debt $9.5B at YE 2025 → $10.7B by 2026-02-23 (post additional secured notes + fiber network term notes); 2025 adj EBITDA $1.17B partial-year; 2026 guide adj EBITDA $1.43-1.48B full-year combined run-rate. Net leverage on the consolidated combined run-rate ~6.5-7.0x; interest coverage on the 2026 ~$775M interest guide is **1.85x — thin**. Equity (UNIT) is up +96% in 6m as the market rewards the fiber-rollup story; bond-side, the same growth narrative carries different weight against the leverage profile.

II. CAPITAL STRUCTURE

- Combined LT debt $9.5B at 2025-12-31; **$10.7B by 2026-02-23** post new secured notes + fiber network term notes (per FY 2025 10-K disclosure).
- Pre-merger Windstream-standalone LT debt was $6.06B at Q2 2025 (last standalone print) — combined entity pulled in legacy Uniti's incremental $3-4B of REIT-level debt + new debt issued at merger close.
- 2025 partial-year adj EBITDA $1.17B (Aug-Dec full-quarter contribution from Windstream + Jan-Jul Uniti standalone); 2026 guide $1.43-1.48B is the first full year combined run-rate.
- Net leverage on consolidated 2026 run-rate: $10.7B / $1.45B = **~7.4x** gross; net of cash (~$240M Q2 2025 standalone WIN + UNIT cash, est. $400-500M combined) = ~6.9-7.0x.
- 2026 interest expense guide $775M; coverage = $1.45B / $0.775B = **1.85x — tight**.
- Tranche stack post-merger: senior secured notes at the consolidated UNIT silo (the merger combined Legacy Uniti and Windstream debt under "a single organizational silo that includes both Uniti and Windstream and their respective subsidiaries, thereby effectively eliminating any debt covenants limiting the ability of Legacy Uniti and Windstream to operate together efficiently" — per UNIT disclosure); secured notes; fiber network term notes (ABS structure, secured by fiber assets); $575M 11% preferred issued at merger close.
- Refi profile: laddered across 2027-2032; 2031 term loan facility was redeemed in early 2026 (per 2026 guide commentary). Material maturities in the 2027-2029 band.
- Liquidity: $400-500M est. cash + revolver; 2026 capex elevated for Kinetic FTTH overbuild + Fiber Infrastructure expansion = limited deleveraging.
- Capital allocation: REIT-era dividend was eliminated at the merger; combined entity is C-corp now, deploying cash into FTTH overbuild + organic fiber expansion.

III. THESIS

The thesis is a dual-track G.W. setup that the equity tape and bond tape are reading differently. The equity story (UNIT +96% 6m, +57% 3m, +26% 1m, $11.83 close at 95% of 52w range, composite **bullish**) is the fiber-rollup rerating: combined entity has $3M+ Kinetic FTTH passings target by 2026 (parallel to OPTU's strategy but in the Windstream legacy footprint of the Southeast/Midwest, where FTTH overbuild is less competed); the merger eliminated the punitive Uniti-Windstream master lease that had been the source of the original 2019 Ch11 bankruptcy; and the combined entity is being positioned as a fiber-infrastructure pure-play that could exit via a private-equity take-out or strategic sale (Brookfield, KKR are repeat infrastructure-fund acquirers in this space). The bond story is the consolidated leverage and coverage burden: $10.7B debt against $1.45B 2026 EBITDA = ~7.4x gross leverage, and 2026 interest expense $775M against $1.45B EBITDA = 1.85x coverage. That's tight by any wireline standard; tight enough that one weak quarter or any 50bps EBITDA miss compresses coverage below 1.7x. G.W.'s heuristic — "distrust media/telecom issuers whose synergies are called out in the second post-merger year" — applies here: the merger only closed Aug 2025; mgmt's $1.43-1.48B 2026 EBITDA guide already assumes meaningful run-rate synergies; if the integration costs run over or the synergies underwhelm in year 1, the EBITDA guide is the variance. The credit-positive offset: the Fiber Infrastructure segment is REIT-style lease income with long-duration contracts (anchor tenant Windstream itself, plus third-party lit services), which supports higher leverage capacity than pure HFC operating cable. Net read: this is a mid-B credit at current leverage, with an embedded option to reprice if the fiber-rollup thesis plays out and combined EBITDA catches up to debt in 2027-2028.

IV. KEY RISKS

- **Synergy underdelivery in year 1.** The 2026 EBITDA guide $1.43-1.48B is the first full year combined run-rate; if synergies or integration savings underwhelm by even $50M, EBITDA misses and coverage drops below 1.8x.
- **Kinetic broadband sub trajectory.** Legacy Windstream Kinetic segment competes with VZ FTTH in some pockets and AT&T Fiber overbuild in the Southeast. Sub losses could accelerate; FTTH counter-build is slower than pure-play overbuilders.
- **Interest expense step-up.** 2026 $775M is the guide; if 2027 debt re-prices into 9-10% paper as the existing maturities roll, interest expense compresses coverage further.
- **Capex intensity for Kinetic FTTH.** The Kinetic FTTH overbuild requires sustained capex; this limits deleveraging from FCF for 2026-2028.
- **Fiber Infrastructure tenant concentration.** The legacy Uniti dark-fiber book has Windstream itself as the anchor tenant (now a related party post-merger, which adds intercompany dynamics). Third-party tenant churn is the variance.
- **REIT-to-C-corp tax structure transition.** Tax-leakage at the consolidated entity reduces FCF available for debt service vs the prior REIT structure.
- **Merger-settlement gain noise.** 2025 net income $1.30B was inflated by a $1.68B one-time merger settlement gain; underlying GAAP run-rate is meaningfully lower.
- **Take-private / LBO risk.** Infrastructure buyer interest is real for fiber assets at this leverage profile; an LBO scenario would likely re-cap the credit in a way that could be either positive (deleveraging) or negative (incremental sponsor debt).

V. RECENT PERFORMANCE

Q4 2025 (printed 2026-03-02 — first full quarter of combined entity): revenue $917.3M, adj EBITDA $365.6M, GAAP net loss -$305.7M (Q4 quarter; includes integration and amortization noise). FY 2025: revenue $2,234.5M, adj EBITDA $1,173.8M (53% margin), net income $1,304.7M (inflated by $1.68B merger settlement gain). LT debt $9.5B at YE 2025; $10.7B by 2026-02-23 after new secured notes + fiber network term notes; redemption of legacy 2031 term loan facility was the offsetting transaction. 2026 guide: revenue $3,605-3,655M, adj EBITDA $1,425-1,475M, GAAP net loss -$(360-410)M, interest expense ~$775M. Equity (UNIT) trading at $11.83 close, **95.0% of 52w range**, 5d +0.7%, 20d +18.2%, 1m +26.1%, 3m +57.3%, 6m +95.9% — composite **bullish**, 90d realized vol 57.4% (74th pct, normal but elevated for a fiber play). The equity ramp confirms the rollup-re-rating thesis on the equity tape; the bond-side question is whether the consolidated 2026 EBITDA delivers the full guided range or comes in at the low end. Q1 2026 print expected early-mid May 2026 (combined-entity full quarter under new reporting structure).

VI. MONITORING TRIGGERS

- **Q1 2026 print (early-mid May 2026):** revenue, adj EBITDA, Kinetic broadband sub trajectory, integration progress vs guide.
- **Combined-entity adj EBITDA:** $1.45B 2026 baseline guide; <$1.40B = thesis miss / synergy underdelivery; >$1.48B = upside surprise.
- **Net leverage trajectory:** ~7.0x baseline; <6.5x by YE 2026 = deleveraging path / >7.5x = leverage building, ratings risk.
- **Interest coverage:** 1.85x baseline; <1.7x at any quarterly print = covenant or rating concern.
- **Kinetic FTTH passings + fiber sub adds:** mgmt has set a multi-year FTTH passings target; quarterly updates show whether the build pace is on track.
- **Refi activity:** any 8-K announcing 2027-2029 secured notes refinancing or new ABS issuance. Pricing of new paper is the credit signal.
- **Integration cost run-rate:** mgmt called out $XX synergies; quarterly updates on whether they're being realized vs deferred.
- **Take-private rumors / 8-K announcements:** infrastructure-fund interest in fiber assets is real; any LBO would re-rate the credit.
